The conjecture states that for any $k \ge 0$, if a $3^+$-parameterized square $w = uv$ with $|u|=|v| \ge 3$ exists as a subword of $x_k$, then $u=v$, meaning there are no non-standard $3^+$-parameterized squares.
proof_strategy: Define the morphisms $\phi$ and $\mu$ on a ternary alphabet. Prove that any parameterized square of length $\ge 6$ in $x_k$ implies $u=v$ by analyzing the local structure around occurrences of 'c' and 'bb', leveraging the fact that $x'_k$ is square-free and the specific substitution properties of $\mu$.
title: Absence of Non-Standard 3+-Parameterized Squares in x_k

description: The regularized coupling of two vector-valued weight 3/2 mock Eisenstein series (which individually yield depth one mock modular forms) produces a depth two mock modular form of weight 3. Specifically, the completion of this coupled object satisfies a $\bar{\partial}$-equation whose shadow is a linear combination of tensor products of depth one mock Eisenstein series and holomorphic modular forms.
proof_strategy: Formalize the definition of depth two mock modular forms and the Eisenstein coupling operator. Compute the Fourier expansion of the coupled series and verify its $\bar{\partial}$-equation using the known analytic properties of mock Eisenstein series and Rankin-Selberg integrals.
title: Depth Two Mock Modularity of Coupled Mock Eisenstein Series

description: For integers $r \ge 2$ and $t_3, \dots, t_{r+1} \ge 2$, the maximum number of edges in a non-$r$-partite $K_{1,1,t_3,\dots,t_{r+1}}$-free graph of order $n$ is exactly $|E(T_{n,r})| - \lfloor n/r \rfloor + 2(t_{\min}-1)$ for all sufficiently large $n$, where $T_{n,r}$ is the Turán graph and $t_{\min} = \min\{t_3,\dots,t_{r+1}\}$.
proof_strategy: Define the non-$r$-partite Turán number, construct the extremal graph by modifying the Turán graph $T_{n,r}$, and prove the upper bound using spectral graph theory and the structural condition on the sub-decomposition family of $K_{1,1,t_3,\dots,t_{r+1}}$.
title: Exact Non-r-Partite Turán Number for Complete Multipartite Graphs

description: In type A_n, the subalgebra B_aff of the affine Hecke algebra admits a canonical basis {b_{W_fin w}} indexed by cosets W_fin \ W_aff. The conjecture states that the structure constants of B_aff with respect to this canonical basis are polynomials in v with non-negative integer coefficients: for any two cosets W_fin w and W_fin w' in W_fin \ W_aff, the product b_{W_fin w} · b_{W_fin w'} = Σ c_{w,w'}^z · b_{W_fin z} where each c_{w,w'}^z ∈ Z_{≥0}[v]. This is the v-deformed analogue of the positivity of structure constants in the affine Fomin-Stanley subalgebra (equivalently, homology of the affine Grassmannian).
proof_strategy: First formalize the affine Weyl group W_aff = W_fin ⋉ Q∨ in type A_n as a Coxeter group with generators S_aff = S_fin ∪ {s_0}. Define the affine Hecke algebra H_aff over Z[v,v^{-1}] with Bernstein presentation and quadratic relations. Construct the pseudo-centralizer subalgebra B_aff as the subalgebra generated by appropriate elements arising from the DAHA centralizer construction. Prove the canonical basis exists (indexed by W_fin \ W_aff) by establishing a graded module structure and applying the bar-involution argument. Finally, establish positivity of structure constants using geometric arguments via the affine Grassmannian or combinatorial arguments via the v-deformed Pieri rule.
title: Positivity of structure constants for the canonical basis of the pseudo-centralizer subalgebra in type A

description: For integers n > l ≥ 2, if E ⊆ ℝⁿ is a Borel set with Hausdorff dimension dim_H(E) > l+1, then for almost every V ∈ G(n,l), the orthogonal projection Π_V(E) has nonempty interior. This improves the Peres–Schlag exponent 2l to l+1, matching the sharp finite-field threshold established in the paper. The case l=1 is excluded since 2l = l+1 = 2 is already sharp by Besicovitch–Mattila constructions. For l ≥ 2, the gap between the known bound 2l and the conjectured bound l+1 remains open, and the paper's finite-field result strongly suggests l+1 is the true threshold.
proof_strategy: The finite-field proof shows the l+1 threshold arises from polynomial method arguments linked to Kakeya set bounds. To lift this to ℝⁿ: (1) discretize the Euclidean problem by replacing E with a δ-packing and passing to a finite-field model via rescaling and reduction mod p, (2) apply the finite-field sharp threshold result to obtain rich projections for the discretized set, (3) use Bourgain's framework reformulating Peres–Schlag in terms of L² bounds for maximal k-plane transforms controlled by Riesz energy, (4) combine with the best available Kakeya maximal L^p estimates (from BCCLXZ and related works) and the paper's maximal k-plane transform bounds to close the gap from 2l down to l+1. Guth's polynomial partitioning method may provide the continuous analogue of the polynomial method used in the finite-field setting.
title: Sharp Euclidean Peres–Schlag Threshold Equals l+1 for l ≥ 2

description: We conjecture that for each integer n≥3 the exponent 3/(2n‑1) in the finite‑field Peres‑Schlag theorem for product sets is optimal. More precisely, there exists a constant c_n > 0 such that for all sufficiently large primes p there is a subset A ⊂ ℤ_p with |A| ≤ c_n·p^{3/(2n‑1)} for which no choice of coefficients t_1,…,t_n ∈ ℤ_p yields a covering t_1A + … + t_nA = ℤ_p. Equivalently, the threshold cannot be lowered below 3/(2n‑1).
proof_strategy: To prove the conjecture one would construct, for each n, small subsets A ⊂ ℤ_p (for large p) that avoid being covered by any n‑term dilated sum. This would likely involve adapting known Kakeya‑type or cap‑set constructions to produce sets whose n‑fold linear images have small density. A successful construction would establish the sharpness of the exponent 3/(2n‑1). A disproof would require showing that any set of size ≈ p^{3/(2n‑1)} inevitably yields a covering, perhaps via Fourier‑analytic or algebraic‑geometric methods.
title: Sharpness of the finite‑field Peres‑Schlag exponent for product sets

description: Every admissible graph (a graph with no pendant path of length two, i.e., no path x-y-z with d(x)=1 and d(y)=2) admits a strong majority edge-coloring with at most 4 colors. A strong majority edge-coloring requires that for every edge e=uv and every color i, at most (d(u)+d(v))/2 - 1 edges adjacent to e receive color i. Kalinowski, Kamyczura, Pilśniak, and Woźniak originally proved 8 colors suffice and conjectured 4; the current paper improves the bound to 5, but the conjecture remains open.
proof_strategy: The case δ(G) ≥ 7 is already settled (4 colors suffice by KKPW). The remaining cases require handling admissible graphs with small minimum degree. A promising approach combines the Hilton–de Werra equitable edge-coloring tools with vertex-splitting arguments used in the 5-color proof, performing a more refined case analysis on the degree structure of low-degree vertices and their local neighborhoods. The key obstacle is ensuring no color dominates the neighborhood of any single edge when restricted to 4 colors.
title: Strong Majority Edge-Coloring Conjecture: Four Colors Suffice for Admissible Graphs

description: For integers $g > k \ge 2$, the prime divisors of the minimal positive multiple $m_k(g)$ of the minimal class $\theta_k$ that is algebraic on a very general principally polarized abelian variety of dimension $g$ are exactly the primes $p \leq (k+1)/2$. This establishes the sharpness of the paper's lower bound, conjecturing that no prime $p > (k+1)/2$ divides $m_k(g)$.
proof_strategy: Extend the combinatorial analysis of $\mathbb{F}_p$-solutions of graphic matroids and their Albanese graphs to prove that no prime $p > (k+1)/2$ can divide $m_k(g)$, thereby establishing the exact equivalence for prime divisibility and confirming the lower bound is sharp.
title: Sharp Primorial Divisibility of Minimal Classes on Abelian Varieties

description: Conjecture: For every P₄‑tidy graph G and any two independent sets I, I' of G with |I| = |I'|, there exists a token‑sliding sequence transforming I into I'. This would extend the polynomial‑time algorithm for the reconfiguration problem on P₄‑tidy graphs to a structural connectivity result for equal‑sized independent sets.
proof_strategy: Use the substitution decomposition (modular decomposition) of P₄‑tidy graphs. Prove the conjecture by induction on the decomposition tree: show that the property holds for prime, parallel, and series nodes, and that token‑sliding moves can be lifted/composed across the decomposition. For prime nodes, exploit the bounded number of P₄’s and the known structure of P₄‑tidy primes to construct explicit sliding sequences.
title: Reachability of equal-size independent sets in P₄‑tidy graphs under token sliding

description: For every elliptic curve E/Q with analytic rank 0 and every non-trivial finite abelian group G, there exist infinitely many G-extensions F/Q such that E(F) is finite (equivalently, rank E(F) = 0). This removes the 'no exceptional primes' condition from the paper's Corollary 1.3 and the 'sufficiently large prime factors' condition from Theorem 1.1, yielding the full generalization of the David-Fearnley-Kisilevsky conjecture from quadratic to all finite abelian extensions.
proof_strategy: The approach should follow the paper's strategy: reduce rank stability to simultaneous non-vanishing of twisted central L-values via Kato's theorem (giving rank upper bounds from analytic rank zero), then establish non-vanishing for all Dirichlet characters in a given group. The key obstacle is removing the 'exceptional prime' and 'sufficiently large prime factor' hypotheses from the horizontal p-adic L-function machinery. This likely requires: (1) refined analysis of local root numbers at all primes dividing the conductor to control the sign in the functional equation uniformly across all twists, and (2) overcoming the limitation that current horizontal p-adic L-function techniques require p to be large relative to the level to ensure Eisenstein-type congruences dominate the residual spectrum.
title: Diophantine Rank Stability for All Abelian Groups

description: Conjecture that for any fixed genus g > 0, there exists a constant C_g > 0 such that the spectral gap γ_{n,g} of the fixed genus chord swap chain on chord diagrams with n chords and genus g satisfies γ_{n,g} ≥ C_g / n for all n > 2g.
proof_strategy: Establish a conductance lower bound via a suitable coupling argument that relates chord swaps to graph-theoretic moves, and then use known inequalities to translate this into a polynomial lower bound on the spectral gap for fixed genus.
title: Polynomial spectral gap lower bound for fixed genus chord swap chain

description: The spectral inequality equivalence for Sidorenko-type inequalities in admissible classes fails for certain bipartite graphs outside the range v(H) ≤ e(H). Specifically, for the 5-vertex path graph H (a tree with 5 vertices and 4 edges), there exists an admissible class C (e.g., the class of doubly nonnegative graphons) such that the spectral inequality holds for all W ∈ C, but H is not C-Sidorenko.
domain_bridges: Spectral radius vs. edge density relationships
proof_strategy: Construct a doubly nonnegative graphon W where the spectral inequality t(H,W) ≥ ρ(W)^{2e(H)-v(H)} p(W)^{v(H)-e(H)} holds but t(H,W) < p(W)^{e(H)} fails, demonstrating the equivalence's optimality in the v(H) ≤ e(H) range.
title: Spectral Transfer Sharpness for Trees Beyond the Sidorenko Range

catalog_references: Grover walk spectral theory –reference to universal Grover‑Ihara polynomial
description: We conjecture that for any monic polynomial P (not necessarily coprime to A^2‑1) the μ‑ and λ‑invariants of the Iwasawa module generated by the spectral resultant R_{X,P} are given by a precise Kida‑type formula involving the p‑adic valuations of R_{X,P} at all torsion characters, with an explicit correction term accounting for the Bass factor A^2‑1. This extends the leading asymptotic growth law proved in the coprime case.
proof_strategy: The proof would proceed by (1) constructing the Iwasawa module M as the Fitting module of the spectral resultant using the universal Grover‑Ihara polynomial; (2) applying the structure theorem for finitely generated Δ_₂[[Γ]]‑modules to express μ(M) and λ(M) in terms of elementary divisors; (3) evaluating the resultant at torsion characters χ∈̀_hat{Δ}_₂^× and showing via equivariant descent that the elementary divisors are precisely the values v_p(R(χ)); (4) incorporating the Bass factor (A^2‑1) by factoring det P(U_n) into a coprime part and a power of the Bass factor, and comparing the resulting contributions to the λ‑term. The key technical step is to prove an equivariant Kida formula for the spectral resultant without integrality assumptions, using the factorization for p‑group covers from the paper and a careful analysis of the local units at χ(1)=±1.
title: Extended μ-λ Formula for Spectral Resultants of Grover Walks on Graph Towers

catalog_references: Dimca, Introduction to Arrangements of Hyperplanes
Dimca & Stríćlaru, Pascal Configurations and Jacobian Syzygies
description: Constructs two nine-line arrangements in \(\mathbb{P}^2\) with isomorphic intersection lattices but distinct minimal degrees of Jacobian relations (mdr). The configurations differ in their homological types, where one is plus-one generated and the other has type 2B, validating distinct Jacobian syzygy structures. The example refutes the conjecture that mdr is combinatorially determined when mdr < d/2.
domain_bridges: Generalized Terao Conjecture and combinatorial invariants
proof_strategy: Explicit construction of arrangements with controlled intersection multiplicities, followed by computation of \(\mdr(f)\) via graded module generation and analysis of Jacobian syzygies using symbolic computation in Lean 4.
title: Minimal Degree of Jacobian Relations for Arrangements with Isomorphic Intersection Lattices

description: The paper proves, assuming the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH), that if K is a totally real Galois number field of degree n ≥ 3 and p is an odd rational prime which does not split completely in K, then every generating set of the ray class group Cl_K^{(p)^N} with modulus (p)^N is a Euclidean system. This conjecture posits that the GRH assumption can be removed, asserting that the statement holds unconditionally.
proof_strategy: The existing proof relies on GRH via Artin's generalized primitive root conjecture to guarantee the existence of primes with specific norm properties that enable the Euclidean division. An unconditional proof would likely require circumventing GRH by developing new analytic number theory techniques to establish stronger lower bounds on the relevant prime counting functions, or by discovering an alternative algebraic mechanism for constructing the Euclidean norm function for ray classes.
title: Unconditional Euclidean Systems for Ray Classes in Totally Real Galois Fields

description: For every n ≥ 0, the n-th row generating function of the square of the Eulerian triangle—defined as the polynomial ∑_k (∑_j A(n,j)·A(j,k)) x^k where A(n,k) is the Eulerian number counting permutations of [n] with k descents—has only real roots. This extends the paper's results on powers of Pascal, Stirling, and Narayana triangles to the still-open Eulerian case.
proof_strategy: Attempt to decompose the Eulerian triangle square as a product of triangles whose individual real-rootedness preservation is known, or extend the rectangular additive convolution framework to construct an interlacing chain for the squared Eulerian row generating functions. Alternatively, establish that the Eulerian triangle square arises from a Narayana-type transformation applied to a suitable real-rooted polynomial.
title: Real-rootedness of the square of the Eulerian triangle

description: For all integers a, b with 3 ≤ a ≤ b, there exists a constant C > 0 such that for any n-vertex graph G that is K_{3,b+1}-free, the number of labeled copies of K_{a,b} in G is at most C * n^3. This captures the main asymptotic upper bound result of the paper, resolving the generalized Turán problem for these parameters.
proof_strategy: Formalize the definitions of K_{s,t}-free graphs and the counting of labeled subgraphs isomorphic to K_{a,b}. Apply the Kővári–Sós–Turán theorem and double counting arguments, bounding the number of K_{a,b} copies by considering the number of common neighbors of a-sets of vertices.
title: Upper Bound on Generalized Turán Number ex(n, K_{a,b}, K_{3,b+1})

description: The sequence of total d-Hoggatt numbers, defined as the row sums H_d(n) = sum_{k=0}^n H_d(n,k), is infinitely log-concave for all d >= 1. The paper proves the infinite log-concavity of the row and column sequences of the d-Hoggatt triangle. However, the infinite log-concavity of the total d-Hoggatt numbers remains open, encompassing the unresolved infinite log-concavity of the Baxter numbers for d=3 and Catalan numbers for d=2.
proof_strategy: Leverage the real-rootedness of the row generating functions (proven by Dilks and Fang-Zhang-Zhao) combined with the theory of multiplier sequences or Pólya frequency sequences to establish the infinite log-concavity of the total sums. Alternatively, employ recurrence relations and induction with tight asymptotic bounds derived from the asymptotic normality of the row sequences.
title: Infinite Log-Concavity of Total d-Hoggatt Numbers

description: For any fixed 0 < q < 1, as the prime modulus r → ∞ and x → ∞ with x ≤ r^{1/2-ε} for fixed ε > 0, the normalized 2q-th moment (1/(r-1))∑_{χ mod r} |∑_{n≤x} χ(n)|^{2q} / x^q converges to an explicit constant C_q equal to the corresponding moment for partial sums of a Steinhaus random multiplicative function. This extends the paper's order-of-magnitude result (which shows the moment is Θ(x^q)) to a precise asymptotic, confirming the heuristic that short character sums behave like random multiplicative functions in the low-moment regime.
proof_strategy: Extend the barrier-adjusted Perron integral comparison method from the current paper to obtain precise asymptotics rather than order-of-magnitude bounds. Key steps: (1) show the barrier adjustment in I(χ) contributes at most o(1) to the normalized moment, allowing direct comparison with the unadjusted integral; (2) establish concentration of the character sum moment around its mean using the fourth moment bounds already developed in the paper; (3) identify the limiting constant via the random multiplicative function model by proving the Euler product structure of the moments converges to the random model value, leveraging the fact that for 0<q<1 the moments are dominated by typical rather than extreme behavior.
title: Asymptotic equivalence of low moments of character sums and random multiplicative sums

description: Let $M$ be a piecewise-linear manifold of dimension $d \ge 1$. If $S$ and $T$ are two locally finite triangulations of $M$, then $S$ and $T$ are related by a locally finite sequence of bistellar moves (Pachner moves).
proof_strategy: Utilize the paper's result that two triangulations with a common subdivision have a common $\omega$-stellar subdivision. Then, show that the $\omega$-stellar subdivision can be reached from the original triangulations via locally finite sequences of bistellar moves, extending Pachner's theorem to infinite complexes by controlling the locality of the inverse stellar moves.
title: Infinite Pachner's Theorem for Locally Finite Triangulations

description: For all positive integers $n$ and $r$, and all partitions $\mu, \lambda \vdash n$, the polynomial $(-1)^{|\mu|-\ell(\mu)}\langle \nabla^r m_\mu, s_\lambda \rangle$ has nonnegative integer coefficients, i.e., belongs to $\mathbb{N}[q,t]$. This generalizes the 1999 conjecture of Bergeron, Garsia, Haiman, and Tesler (which corresponds to the case $r=1$), recently proven in the paper.
proof_strategy: Formalize the ring of symmetric functions, the Hall inner product, and the modified Macdonald basis. Define the nabla operator and the Haglund-Morse-Zabrocki operators $C_\alpha$. Establish the expansion of $(-1)^{|\mu|-\ell(\mu)}m_\mu$ in the $C_\alpha(1)$ basis with nonnegative coefficients in $\mathbb{Q}_{\ge 0}[q]$. Finally, combine this expansion with the compositional shuffle theorem and the Schur positivity of LLT polynomials to conclude the nonnegativity of the inner product.
title: Generalized BGHT Signed Schur Positivity Conjecture

catalog_references: Fair Allocation under Conflict Constraints via Strong Colorability (ArXiv)
description: For every integer Δ ≥ 1, there exists a graph G with maximum degree Δ such that the minimum number of agents required to guarantee an SD-EF1 allocation for common preferences is exactly 3Δ - 1.
proof_strategy: Construct an explicit family of graphs with maximum degree Δ whose first-level strong chromatic number (which characterizes SD-EF1) equals 3Δ - 1, using the hierarchy of strong chromatic number variants introduced in the paper. Verify that no SD-EF1 allocation exists for fewer than 3Δ - 1 agents by leveraging the exact characterization of SD-EF1 in terms of this graph parameter.
title: Tightness of the 3Δ - 1 Bound for SD-EF1 Allocations

description: The Extended 1-2-3 Conjecture posits that for any finite nonempty set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ and any positive integer $n$, the symmetric difference $A \Delta 2A \Delta \cdots \Delta nA$ contains at least $n$ elements. While recently proven for all $n$ sufficiently large (specifically $n \ge 2(3^{80}-321)$) and for $n \le 6$, the conjecture remains open in general, particularly for intermediate values of $n$.
proof_strategy: Formalize the known small cases ($n \le 6$) and the asymptotic result, then bridge the remaining gap $7 \le n < 2(3^{80}-321)$ by either refining the analytic bounds on rough numbers to lower the constant $N$, or developing new combinatorial arguments for intermediate values of $n$.
title: Extended 1-2-3 Conjecture for Symmetric Differences

description: For p an odd prime, k ≥ 2 an even integer, and a_p in the algebraic closure of Q_p with v(a_p) > 0 and v(a_p) not an integer (i.e., the slope is fractional), the mod p semisimplified reduction V̄_{k,a_p} of the two-dimensional crystalline representation V_{k,a_p} of G_{Q_p} is irreducible. This folklore conjecture is partially established in the paper for fractional slopes less than p-2 and sufficiently large even weights k under a slope assumption on bad congruence classes of k mod p.
proof_strategy: First formalize filtered phi-modules and the equivalence between crystalline representations and admissible filtered phi-modules (Fontaine's theory). Then build the mod p local Langlands correspondence for GL_2(Q_p) in Lean, establishing the correspondence between Galois representations and representations of GL_2(F_p). The irreducibility for even weight and fractional slope follows by analyzing which mod p representations of GL_2(Q_p) can arise via the correspondence, showing that reducible reductions correspond to integer slopes when k is even.
title: Irreducibility of mod p reductions of crystalline representations at fractional slope and even weight

description: The paper proves that the average absolute character sum over y-smooth numbers is o(√Ψ(x,y)) when q ≥ x^{1+ε}. This conjecture asserts that the same sub-square-root bound holds at the critical threshold q ≥ x (i.e., ε = 0), with a concrete saving factor. Specifically: for every ε > 0, there exists x₀(ε) such that for all x ≥ x₀, all primes q ≥ x, and all y with (log x)⁶ ≤ y ≤ x^{1/(32 log log x)}, the average absolute smooth character sum satisfies (1/(q-1)) Σ_{χ mod q, χ≠χ₀} |Σ_{n≤x, P(n)≤y} χ(n)| ≤ (1−ε)√Ψ(x,y). This extends the paper's main theorem from q ≥ x^{1+ε} to the boundary case q ≥ x, which is the natural threshold where the problem transitions from trivial to nontrivial.
proof_strategy: Adapt the paper's connection between character sums and Steinhaus random multiplicative functions. The key step is establishing the moment identity (1/φ(q))Σ_χ|Σ_{n≤x,P(n)≤y}χ(n)|^{2k} = E|Σ_{n≤x,P(n)≤y,(n,q)=1}f(n)|^{2k} for q ≥ x, which requires careful treatment of the coprimality condition at the boundary. Then leverage the authors' prior result on random multiplicative functions over smooths to extract the sub-square-root saving, combined with Harper's hypercontractivity machinery to control higher moments at the critical regime.
title: Sub-square-root bound for smooth character sums at the critical threshold

description: For every fixed graph H that contains at least one edge, the decision problem Chromatic Sum remains NP‑complete when restricted to H‑free graphs (i.e., graphs that do not contain H as a subgraph). This conjecture is falsifiable because a single counterexample—a graph class H‑free for which Chromatic Sum is polynomial‑time solvable— would refute it.
proof_strategy: Establish NP‑membership in NP and prove NP‑hardness via a reduction from a known NP‑complete problem (e.g., 3‑Partition) while respecting the H‑free restriction.
title: Chromatic Sum is NP-complete on H‑free graphs for any fixed graph H with at least one edge

description: For any primitive holomorphic cusp form f of even weight k ≥ 2 for Γ₀(N), at least 1/3 of the zeros of the family of twisted L-functions L(s, f × χ) lie on the critical line Re(s) = 1/2, where χ ranges over primitive Dirichlet characters of conductor ≤ Q as Q → ∞. This extends the paper's positive-proportion result for PGL(2) (which likely yields ~1/9 via Levinson's method with current mollifier lengths) to the expected optimal proportion, analogous to Levinson's classical 1/3 result for the Riemann zeta function. The proportion is defined as liminf_{Q→∞} N_{crit}(f, Q) / N_{total}(f, Q) where N_{crit} counts zeros on Re(s)=1/2 and N_{total} counts zeros in the critical strip across the family.
proof_strategy: Adapt Levinson's zero-detection method with optimized multi-parameter mollifiers for the family L(s, f × χ), leveraging the paper's asymptotic large sieve with power-saving error terms for PGL(2) twisted L-functions. The key bottleneck is constructing mollifiers of sufficient length—current techniques using the paper's mean value theorem with θ=0 error term O(Q^{7/4+ε}) yield a smaller proportion. Achieving 1/3 requires either: (1) extending the allowable mollifier length θ beyond 1/2−ε in the mean value theorem, or (2) developing a twisted analogue of Conrey's refinements to Levinson's method, using the extra averaging over χ to absorb longer mollifiers. The unconditional nature of the PGL(2) results (no GRC needed) makes this approach viable.
title: One-Third Proportion Conjecture for Critical Zeros of GL(2) Twisted L-functions

description: Conjecture: Any arithmetic function f : ℕ → ℂ with |f(n)| ≤ 1 for all n, satisfying a completed L-function functional equation Λ_f(s)=ε Λ_f(1-s) for some root of unity ε, and assuming that the minimal conductor N>1 is such that the support of f is contained in {1,…,N}, must be a primitive Dirichlet character modulo N. In particular f must be completely multiplicative, have absolute value 1 on coprime arguments, and its order must divide the parity of ε.
proof_strategy: Apply Mellin transform techniques to the Dirichlet series ∑ f(n)/n^s to derive analytic continuation and functional equation constraints; then use Fourier analysis on finite abelian groups to show that boundedness and the functional equation force multiplicativity and character-like behaviour.
title: Functional Equations Characterize Primitive Dirichlet Characters

description: A connected reductive group G over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic p > 0 admits a Springer isomorphism (a G-equivariant isomorphism between the unipotent variety and the nilpotent cone) if and only if for every unipotent element u in G(k), the centralizer Z_G(u) is smooth. The paper establishes that PGL_p in characteristic p has non-smooth unipotent centralizers and no Springer isomorphism; this conjecture posits these two phenomena are equivalent in general.
proof_strategy: The 'only if' direction: show that a Springer isomorphism maps each unipotent centralizer isomorphically onto the corresponding nilpotent stabilizer, and nilpotent stabilizers are always smooth for reductive groups in good characteristic. The 'if' direction: use the smoothness of all unipotent centralizers to construct the isomorphism via the Dynkin-Spaltenstein construction, ensuring the scheme-theoretic conditions are satisfied. Lean formalization would require developing the theory of unipotent varieties, nilpotent cones, G-equivariant morphisms of schemes, and smoothness criteria for group scheme centralizers.
title: Springer Isomorphism Characterization via Centralizer Smoothness

description: For any integers 2 ≤ s < t and any n-vertex graph G, the t-clique density of G is bounded below by the composition of the Lovász-Simonovits t-clique density function evaluated at the generalized inverse of the s-clique density function applied to the s-clique density of G. Specifically, k_t(G) / n^t ≥ F_t(F_s^{-1}(k_s(G) / n^s)). This encompasses Reiher's clique density theorem as a special case when s=2.
proof_strategy: First, formalize Turán graphs and compute their s-clique and r-clique counts to establish the critical points. Define the piecewise linear function L_{s,r} and prove Bollobás's original piecewise-linear interpolation bound. Define the Lovász-Simonovits clique density function F_r and its generalized inverse F_s^{-1}. Finally, formalize the inductive proof strategy presented in the paper, showing that the piecewise-linear bound is superseded by the continuous bound involving F_t and F_s^{-1}.
title: Asymptotic Clique-to-Clique Density Bound

description: The main result establishing the exact exponential growth rate of the ρ-th moment of constrained guesswork G_coset for a random binary linear code of rate R under i.i.d. Bernoulli(p) noise. It demonstrates that the exponent shifts down by exactly ρ(1-R) relative to the unconstrained Arıkan--Merhav exponent, yielding a closed-form limit expressed in terms of the binary Rényi entropy.
proof_strategy: Define the probability space for random binary linear codes and the constrained guesswork rank. Prove the universality theorem, expressing the guesswork exponent as a functional of the weight-enumerator growth rate: (1+ρ)ψ_{1/(1+ρ)}(g) - ρψ_1(g). Then, evaluate this Legendre-type transform for the specific weight-enumerator growth rate of random linear codes to derive the closed-form exponent ρ h_{1/(1+ρ)}(p) + ρ(R-1).
title: Exact Exponent for Constrained Coset Guesswork

description: For any integer $g \ge 2$, let $d \in \{2g+1, 2g+2\}$, $\alpha \in \mathbb{Z} \setminus \{0\}$, and let $p$ be a prime such that $p > P^+(d)$ and $p \nmid \alpha$, where $P^+(d)$ is the bound from the paper ($d^2-4d+2$ if $d$ is odd, $(d^2-3d+2)/2$ if $d$ is even). Let $M(t)$ be the $g \times g$ Cartier-Manin matrix of the hyperelliptic curve $y^2 = x^d + \alpha x + t$ over $\mathbb{F}_p$. The determinant $\det(M(t))$ is a nonzero polynomial in $\mathbb{F}_p[t]$.
proof_strategy: Define the Cartier-Manin matrix entries as coefficients of the polynomial $(x^d + \alpha x + t)^{(p-1)/2}$, compute its determinant as a polynomial in $t$, and show that its degree and leading coefficient modulo $p$ imply nonvanishing, leveraging the bounds on $p$-adic valuations of the terms which hold precisely when $p > P^+(d)$ and $p \nmid \alpha$.
title: Nonvanishing of Cartier-Manin Determinant for Generic Hyperelliptic Families

description: For a geometric family of principally polarized abelian varieties over Q, the average size of the ℓ-Selmer group is unbounded if and only if the product of local Tamagawa ratios exceeds 1. Specifically, for the family of quadratic twists {E_d : d squarefree} of an elliptic curve E/Q at a prime ℓ of good reduction, the average |Sel_ℓ(E_d)| over |d| ≤ X is unbounded as X → ∞ if and only if ∏_p c_p(E, ℓ) > 1, where c_p(E, ℓ) is the local factor from the Greenberg–Wiles formula. The paper proves this for families with constant ℓ-torsion Galois module; the conjecture asserts it holds unconditionally.
proof_strategy: Reduce to the constant ℓ-torsion case by analyzing how the local Tamagawa ratios c_p vary across the family. Use the Greenberg-Wiles formula to express |Sel_ℓ(A)|/|Sel_ℓ(A^∨)^∨| = ∏_p c_p. For principally polarized varieties, the Cassels pairing gives |Sel_ℓ(A)| ≥ √(∏_p c_p). The key step is showing that the dual Selmer correction factor is bounded on average across the family, using the character sum and ramification section machinery developed in the paper to control the discrepancy between the local lower bound and the true Selmer size.
title: Tamagawa Ratio Criterion for Unbounded Selmer Moments

description: The paper proves that a countable FAC poset P satisfies the Aharoni-Korman conjecture if P contains no saturated chain D such that either D or its reverse D* is of the form ⊕_{x∈ω} D_x, where each D_x is infinite and co-wellfounded. The conjecture asserts that this condition is also necessary: if a countable FAC poset P does contain such a saturated chain, then P fails to satisfy the Aharoni-Korman conjecture. This would yield a complete characterization of which countable FAC posets satisfy the Aharoni-Korman conjecture.
proof_strategy: Construct an explicit countable FAC poset P containing a saturated chain of the forbidden form, then show that no chain in P can simultaneously meet every antichain in any antichain partition of P. The construction likely involves adapting the known counterexamples to the original Aharoni-Korman conjecture, using the specific structure of ⊕_{x∈ω} D_x to control all possible chain-antichain interactions.
title: Necessity of the forbidden chain condition for the Aharoni-Korman conjecture on countable FAC posets

description: For a squarefree integer N > 1 with an even number of prime factors, and a positive divisor d | N, let w_d denote the corresponding Atkin-Lehner involution on the Shimura curve X_N. The genus of the quotient X_N / ⟨w_d⟩ is determined by the Riemann-Hurwitz formula applied to the double cover X_N → X_N / ⟨w_d⟩, where the number of fixed points of w_d equals the number of optimal embeddings of a certain quadratic order into the quaternion order, expressible via class numbers. The conjecture is: X_N / ⟨w_d⟩ has genus zero if and only if (N, d) belongs to an explicit finite list, which strictly contains the list {(6,6), (10,10), (22,22)} arising from genus-zero X_N alone. This classification is the key structural result enabling the extension of the Giampietro-Darmon factorization beyond the original conjecture.
proof_strategy: First formalize the genus formula for Shimura curves X_N of discriminant N (already explicit in the literature, e.g., Ogg). Then formalize the fixed-point count of Atkin-Lehner involutions w_d in terms of class numbers of imaginary quadratic orders via optimal embedding counts. Apply Riemann-Hurwitz to the double cover X_N → X_N/⟨w_d⟩ to obtain the genus of the quotient. Finally, enumerate all pairs (N, d) with N squarefree, ω(N) even, d | N, for which the resulting genus is zero, yielding the explicit finite classification.
title: Genus-Zero Classification of Atkin-Lehner Quotients of Shimura Curves

description: Every symmetric edge polytope of dimension at most 35 has a gamma-positive Ehrhart h*-polynomial; equivalently, 36 is the minimum dimension in which a symmetric edge polytope can fail to be gamma-positive. This is motivated by the paper's construction of a 36-dimensional counterexample to the Ohsugi-Tsuchiya conjecture and by extensive computational evidence for small graphs.
proof_strategy: Combine exhaustive computational verification for graphs on few vertices with structural graph-theoretic arguments showing that any counterexample to gamma-positivity must arise from graphs with sufficiently complex series-parallel structure (specifically, requiring at least 5 parallel paths of length at least 8), thereby establishing a minimum vertex count and hence minimum dimension threshold.
title: Gamma-positivity threshold for symmetric edge polytopes

catalog_references: Polynomial mixing for polygonal side matchings
description: The paper establishes that the diameter of the connected component of the chord swap graph on chord diagrams of size n and genus g (for n > 2g) is bounded above by C(n + g^2) for some universal constant C > 0. We conjecture that this universal constant can be taken to be exactly 1, yielding a tight diameter upper bound of precisely n + g^2.
proof_strategy: Construct explicit short paths between any two chord diagrams by defining a canonical minimal genus diagram and showing that any diagram can be reduced to this canonical form in at most (n + g^2)/2 swaps. This would establish the diameter bound via the triangle inequality. Alternatively, use structural induction on n and g, verifying that the bound holds for base cases and that any valid chord swap preserves the bound.
title: Optimal Diameter Bound for Fixed Genus Chord Swap Graphs

description: For any simple graph G with maximum degree Delta(G) > |V(G)|/3, the chromatic index of G is Delta(G) if and only if G contains no Delta(G)-overfull subgraph. Equivalently, if Delta(G) > |V(G)|/3 and G contains no Delta(G)-overfull subgraph, then G is class 1.
proof_strategy: Assume G is class 2, meaning chi'(G) = Delta(G) + 1. Analyze the structure of critical subgraphs. Show that a Delta-critical graph with Delta > n/3 must contain an overfull subgraph, deriving a contradiction to the assumption that no overfull subgraph exists.
title: Overfull Conjecture

description: The maximum of the logarithm of the absolute value of the Riemann zeta function on the critical line over the interval [T, 2T], defined as M_T = max_{t ∈ [T, 2T]} log|ζ(1/2 + it)|, satisfies the convergence in distribution: M_T - log(log(T)) + (3/2)log(log(log(T))) converges to the sum of two independent Gumbel random variables as T → ∞. This captures the extreme value statistics of the number-theoretic analogue to the black hole microstate counts proposed in the paper.
proof_strategy: Model the Riemann zeta function as the characteristic polynomial of a random unitary matrix, establish a Gaussian multiplicative chaos representation for the field, and extend the Circular Unitary Ensemble (CUE) maximum theorem to the number theory setting using correlations of zeros.
title: Fyodorov-Hiary-Keating Conjecture for the Riemann Zeta Function

description: For any split connected reductive group G over Q_p with Borel subgroup B and maximal torus T, the trianguline variety Y^{tri}(G) is Cohen-Macaulay. This strengthens the normality results established by Breuil-Hellmann-Schraen (for GL_n) and generalized in this paper (to arbitrary split reductive G, at certain points outside the smooth locus). Since Y^{tri}(G) is smooth of dimension dim(B) = dim(T) + |Φ^+| over the regular locus, Cohen-Macaulayness would follow from Serre's criterion (S2) combined with (R1) regularity in codimension 1. The (S2) condition is the deeper claim: for every point x ∈ Y^{tri}(G) with local ring O_{Y^{tri},x}, and every regular sequence f_1,...,f_d in the maximal ideal, the quotient O_{Y^{tri},x}/(f_1,...,f_d) has depth exactly d. This would imply the existence of well-behaved dualizing complexes and resolve the singularities of Y^{tri}(G) in the sense of local Langlands.
proof_strategy: Step 1: Formalize the trianguline variety Y^{tri}(G) as a rigid analytic space parameterizing trianguline G-representations with their triangulation data, using the Tannakian formalism for Rep_L(G) developed in the paper. Step 2: Establish that Y^{tri}(G) is regular in codimension ≤ 1 (condition R1) by analyzing the singular locus—its complement is the smooth regular locus characterized by the regularity of the triangulation parameter δ: T(Z_p) → T(E), and the singular locus has codimension ≥ 2 by dimension counting via the root structure of G. Step 3: Prove condition (S2) by showing that for every point x with codim ≥ 2, the local ring O_{Y^{tri},x} satisfies depth ≥ min(2, dim O_{Y^{tri},x}), using the crystallinity criterion for (φ,Γ)-modules with G-structure established in the paper to control the local equations. Step 4: Apply Serre's criterion (R1 + S2 ⟹ normal + CM for equidimensional schemes) to conclude.
title: Cohen-Macaulay Property of the Trianguline Variety for Reductive Groups

description: Every well-founded partially ordered set satisfying the finite antichain condition (FAC) has the Aharoni-Korman property: there exists a chain C and a partition of the poset into antichains such that C intersects every antichain in the partition. The paper proves the Aharoni-Korman conjecture for countable FAC posets avoiding a specific chain obstruction (saturated chains of the form ⊕_{x∈ω} D_x with each D_x infinite and co-wellfounded). This conjecture extends the result to all well-founded FAC posets, regardless of cardinality, since well-foundedness eliminates infinite descending obstructing chains and structurally constrains ascending ones.
proof_strategy: Stratify the well-founded poset by rank into well-ordered levels. Apply the paper's countable decomposition and scattered poset analysis within each stratum. Use transfinite induction on the rank function to construct the witnessing chain and antichain partition globally, ensuring the chain meets every antichain in the partition at each inductive stage. The key insight is that well-foundedness provides a rank function that naturally organizes the construction and prevents the specific chain obstruction identified in the paper.
title: Aharoni-Korman Property for Well-Founded FAC Posets

description: For the family of series-parallel graphs G(a) obtained by joining two distinguished vertices s and t with m disjoint paths of lengths a_1, ..., a_m, the paper shows that gamma-positivity of the h*-polynomial of Q_G fails for m >= 5. The conjecture is that for m <= 4, gamma-positivity always holds: for every vector a in Z_{>=1}^4, the h*-polynomial of Q_{G(a)} is gamma-positive. This would yield a complete classification of gamma-positivity for this family.
proof_strategy: For m <= 3, leverage known results: graphs with a vertex connected to all others (cones) are gamma-positive by Ohsugi-Tsuchiya, and complete bipartite graphs by Higashitani-Jochemko-Michalek. For m = 4, compute the gamma-polynomial coefficients using the regular unimodular triangulation structure of symmetric edge polytopes and show all coefficients are non-negative. The linear and quadratic gamma-coefficients are already known positive; the key is controlling the cubic and higher terms via the combinatorics of the series-parallel structure.
title: Gamma-positivity of symmetric edge polytopes for series-parallel graphs with at most four paths

description: For every simple graph G with maximum degree Δ(G) > |V(G)|/3, the chromatic index χ'(G) equals Δ(G) if and only if G contains no Δ(G)-overfull subgraph (a subgraph H with |E(H)| > Δ(G)·⌊|V(H)|/2⌋). This would yield a polynomial-time algorithm for determining the chromatic index of dense graphs and implies several longstanding conjectures including the 1-Factorization Conjecture for regular graphs.
proof_strategy: First formalize the core graph-theoretic infrastructure (chromatic index, overfull subgraphs, critical graphs). Prove key lemmas: (1) any Δ-overfull subgraph forces class 2, (2) the Petersen-minus-vertex P* is class 2 with no 3-overfull subgraph (showing Δ > |V|/3 is tight), (3) reduction to Δ-critical graphs. Then apply structural decomposition of critical graphs with Δ > |V|/3 to show they must contain overfull subgraphs, extending known results from Δ ≥ |V|−2 inward.
title: The Overfull Conjecture

description: The maximum fluctuation of log-microstate counts log Ω_N(E) over energy intervals of width O(√E) in large-N AdS/CFT belongs to the Fyodorov-Hiary-Keating universality class of Gaussian log-correlated fields. Specifically, defining M_N = max_{E ∈ [E₀, E₀ + δ]} log Ω_N(E) with δ ∝ √E₀ and E₀ ∝ N² (the black hole mass scale), the rescaled maximum (M_N - μ_N)/σ_N converges in distribution to a random variable with the modified Gumbel cumulative distribution function exp(-K·exp(-s)), where μ_N = (1/2)·S_N·log(S_N), σ_N = log(S_N), S_N ∝ N² is the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy, and K > 0 is a universal constant determined by the log-correlated field covariance structure. This modified Gumbel with logarithmic correction factors distinguishes the FHK universality class from the classical Gumbel extreme value distribution and parallels the original FHK conjecture for max_t log|ζ(1/2+it)| on [0,T].
proof_strategy: Establish the Gaussian log-correlated field structure of log Ω_N(E) via the holographic dictionary, identifying the covariance Cov(log Ω_N(E), log Ω_N(E')) ∼ log(N/|E-E'|) for nearby energies. Then apply the branching random walk / Gaussian multiplicative chaos framework to characterize the maximum: (1) prove the sub-leading order maximum concentrates via second moment method on the 'peaks' landscape of the log-correlated field; (2) establish the modified Gumbel tail by showing the maximum over dyadic mesoscopic intervals factorizes asymptotically (the decorrelation property); (3) identify the constant K via the local limit theorem for the number of high peaks. The key technical bridge is the equivalence between erratic N-dependence in AdS/CFT and the decorrelation of independent copies of the Gaussian model.
title: FHK Universality Class for Black Hole Microstate Extreme Values

description: While White's conjecture on symmetric exchanges (Part 2) is false, the weaker Part 3 remains open: for any matroid M and any two multisets of bases B and B' with the same multiset union of elements, it is possible to obtain B' from B by repeatedly replacing two bases with any two other bases having the same multiset union. This is equivalent to the toric ideal of the matroid basis exchange ring being generated by quadratic binomials.
proof_strategy: The conjecture could be approached by demonstrating that the toric ideal of any matroid basis exchange ring is generated by quadratic binomials. One could use tropical geometry or Gröbner basis techniques, or attempt an inductive proof on matroid minors, extending the methods used for specific matroid classes like uniform or graphic matroids.
title: White's Quadratic Exchange Conjecture (Part 3)

description: The trianguline variety X^{tri}_G associated to a split connected reductive group G over a p-adic field K is Cohen-Macaulay. Specifically, for every point x in X^{tri}_G with local ring O_{X^{tri}_G,x}, the depth equals the Krull dimension: depth(O_{X^{tri}_G,x}) = dim(O_{X^{tri}_G,x}). This extends the paper's results establishing smoothness on the very regular locus and normality at certain points outside this locus, predicting that all singularities are as mild as possible. Cohen-Macaulayness would imply full normality of X^{tri}_G (since CM implies Serre's condition S2, and the smooth locus has complement of codimension ≥ 2 by the regularity conditions on the triangulation parameter), strengthening the paper's partial normality result. It would also have significant consequences for the deformation theory of p-adic Galois representations with G-structure and for understanding the local Langlands correspondence via the geometry of the trianguline variety.
proof_strategy: The proof would proceed by analyzing the local structure of the trianguline variety at each point. Key steps: (1) On the very regular locus, the variety is smooth (proven in the paper), hence Cohen-Macaulay. (2) At singular points, use the Tannakian formalism developed in the paper to reduce to understanding the tangent cone in terms of root data. (3) The tangent cone at a singular point with parameter δ should be controlled by the roots α for which δ∘α∨ fails to be regular—these correspond to the walls of the Weyl chambers where smoothness breaks down. (4) Show that the defining ideal at each point is generated by a regular sequence of length equal to the codimension, leveraging the crystallinity criterion from the paper to explicitly describe the deformation ring. (5) The root system combinatorics (specifically, the Chevalley commutation relations and the structure of the unipotent radical) should ensure the regular sequence property holds via an inductive argument on the height of r
title: Cohen-Macaulayness of the Trianguline Variety for Reductive Groups

description: For a prime p ≠ 2, a finite extension K of Q_p, and a set T = {a₀, b₀, ..., aᵍ, bᵍ} ⊂ P¹(K) of size 2g+2 with g ≥ 1, the set T is in good position (meaning Γ(T) = ⟨s₀,...,sᵍ⟩ is discontinuous and equals the free product ⟨s₀⟩*...*⟨sᵍ⟩, where each sᵢ has order 2 with fixed points {aᵢ,bᵢ}) if and only if: (1) the tree T(T) constructed from the reduction data is a path graph of length 2g+1, and (2) the p-adic valuations of the off-diagonal entries of normalized representatives of the sᵢ satisfy explicit contraction bounds ensuring the generators act as sufficiently contracting maps on the respective complementary residue disks in the Bruhat-Tits tree of PGL₂(K).
proof_strategy: The forward direction (necessity) follows from the paper's Lemma establishing that good position implies the tree T(T) has the required path structure. The backward direction (sufficiency) requires showing that when T(T) is a path of length 2g+1 and the contraction bounds hold, the group Γ(T) is free on the generators sᵢ: one analyzes the action on the Bruhat-Tits tree of PGL₂(K), showing that the contraction conditions force each reduced word in the sᵢ to act without fixed points in Ω_Γ, precluding any relations beyond sᵢ² = 1. The p-adic analytic estimates on matrix entries control how far the generators move points in the Bruhat-Tits tree, ensuring that compositions cannot create accidental fixed points.
title: Tree-Contraction Characterization of Good Position for p-adic Schottky Groups

description: For a finite poset P, the probabilistic powerdomain V1(P) is an RB-domain if and only if the local stochastic cone at every point of V1(P) is simplicial. This conjecture provides a geometric characterization of the RB-property that is equivalent to the combinatorial condition (P has a least element and its undirected Hasse graph is a tree) proven in the paper. It is falsifiable because one could exhibit a finite poset whose probabilistic powerdomain is an RB-domain but has a non-simplicial stochastic cone at some point, or vice versa.
proof_strategy: The paper's Euclidean finite-step cone argument shows that a cycle in the Hasse graph makes the local stochastic cone non-simplicial, which obstructs the existence of the directed family of deflations required for an RB-domain. For the converse, assuming all stochastic cones are simplicial, one must construct a directed family of deflations with finite image approximating the identity. This could be done by projecting onto faces of the probability simplex corresponding to down-sets of P, using the tree structure implied by the simplicial cone condition.
title: Simplicial Stochastic Cone Characterization of RB-Domains in Probabilistic Powerdomains

description: The Giampietro-Darmon factorization formula for the norm of $p$-adic cross-ratios of CM points on Atkin-Lehner quotients of Shimura curves, currently proven only for genus 0 quotients, holds unconditionally for all squarefree $N > 1$ with an even number of prime factors. For quotients of higher genus, the infinite product of $p$-adic cross-ratios factors into a product of local intersection multiplicities of the corresponding Heegner divisors, up to a global obstruction given by the Néron-Tate height pairing on the Jacobian.
proof_strategy: Generalize the $p$-adic uniformization to higher genus quotients by considering the rigid analytic Jacobian, relate the $p$-adic cross-ratios to the Néron-Tate height pairing of Heegner divisors, and apply the $p$-inverted Howard-Yang counting problem to compute the local intersection multiplicities, thereby reducing the arbitrary genus case to the genus 0 case via a height decomposition.
title: Generalized Giampietro-Darmon Factorization for Arbitrary Genus

description: The main theorem of the paper: Let N > 1 be a squarefree integer with an even number of prime factors, and let p be a prime divisor of N. The factorization formula for the norm of the p-adic cross-ratio infinite product of CM points on the Shimura curve X_N holds if the Atkin-Lehner quotient X_N / w_p has genus 0. This extends the original Giampietro-Darmon conjecture, which required the Shimura curve X_N itself to have genus 0 (a condition only satisfied for N in {6, 10, 22}).
proof_strategy: First formalize the definition of indefinite rational quaternion algebras, maximal orders, and the corresponding Shimura curves X_N over the rationals. Define the Atkin-Lehner involutions and compute the genus of the quotients X_N / w_p. Then construct the p-adic upper half plane, CM points, and the p-adic cross-ratio infinite product. Finally, connect the genus zero condition of the quotient to the p-inverted Howard-Yang counting problem to derive the explicit factorization of the norm.
title: Atkin-Lehner Genus Zero Criterion for Giampietro-Darmon Factorization

description: Every symmetric edge polytope of dimension at most 35 has a γ-positive Ehrhart h*-polynomial. Equivalently, 36 is the minimum dimension of a symmetric edge polytope whose Ehrhart h*-polynomial fails to be γ-positive. This would sharpen the paper's existence result by establishing the exact threshold, confirming that no smaller counterexamples to the Ohsugi–Tsuchiya conjecture exist.
proof_strategy: Combine exhaustive computational verification of γ-positivity for all connected graphs on at most 9 vertices (covering dimensions ≤ 8) with structural arguments that γ-positivity is preserved under cone, join, and subdivision operations, thereby inductively covering all dimensions up to 35 while using the paper's explicit 36-dimensional counterexample as the lower bound.
title: Dimension Threshold for Gamma-Positivity of Symmetric Edge Polytopes

description: For the fixed genus chord swap Markov chain on chord diagrams with n chords and genus g, the spectral gap γ_{n,g} satisfies γ_{n,g} = Θ(n^{-3}) when g is fixed and n → ∞. This sharpens the paper's polynomial lower bound to a precise exponent and matches the n^{-3} scaling observed in related swap chains on perfect matchings.
proof_strategy: First formalize chord diagrams, genus via Euler characteristic, and the chord swap relation in Lean. Then establish the O(n^{-3}) upper bound on the spectral gap via comparison with the random transposition walk on matchings, and prove the Ω(n^{-3}) lower bound by constructing a canonical path argument with congestion bounded by O(n^3), extending the paper's coupling/canonical-path techniques.
title: Tight spectral gap exponent for the fixed-genus chord swap chain

description: The cyclotomic matrix $A_k(\chi) = [G_N(\chi^{ki+kj})]$ involving Gauss sums over $\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$ (where $N=p^m$ and $n=\varphi(N)/k$) can be decomposed as the matrix product $W D W^T$, where $W$ is the $n \times n$ discrete Fourier transform matrix with entries $W_{i,a} = \omega^{ai}$ ($\omega$ being a primitive $n$-th root of unity) and $D$ is the diagonal matrix of the $n$ Gauss periods $\eta_a$ corresponding to the $k$-th power residue cyclotomic cosets.
proof_strategy: Rewrite the Gauss sum $G_N(\chi^{k(i+j)})$ by partitioning the summation over $(\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})^\times$ into the $n$ cyclotomic cosets $C_a$ modulo $k$. Express $\chi^{k(i+j)}(x)$ as $\omega^{a(i+j)}$ for $x \in C_a$, pulling the root of unity out of the sum to yield $\sum_{a=0}^{n-1} \omega^{a(i+j)} \eta_a$, which directly translates to the matrix factorization $A_k(\chi) = W D W^T$.
title: Factorization of Cyclotomic Gauss Sum Matrix

description: For any graph of order n ≥ 8, if it contains strictly more than T(n) = (n^2 - 3n)/2 - ⌈n/2⌉ + 2 edges, then every edge in the graph has strictly positive Ollivier/Lin-Lu-Yau curvature.
proof_strategy: Formalize the Lin-Lu-Yau curvature using the 1-Wasserstein distance between probability measures on vertices. Establish structural properties of graphs with non-positive curvature edges, and demonstrate that exceeding the edge threshold T(n) precludes the existence of such subgraphs, thereby forcing all edge curvatures to be strictly positive.
title: Positive Curvature Threshold for Lin-Lu-Yau Curvature

description: For all finite graphs F and G, there exists an oddomorphism from F to G if and only if G is a split-off minor of F. The forward direction is established in the paper; the converse remains open.
proof_strategy: The forward direction is given by the paper's Theorem that oddomorphism from F to G implies G is a split-off minor of F. For the converse, attempt to construct an oddomorphism from F to G given that G is a split-off minor of F, by reversing each split-off minor operation step and verifying parity conditions on homomorphism counts are preserved. A counterexample search via CFI-type constructions could also be pursued.
title: Equivalence of Oddomorphism and Split-Off Minor

description: For every positive integer n and positive reals α, β with αβ = π², the alternating Hurwitz zeta function ζ_E(s, x) = Σ_{k=0}^∞ (-1)^k / (k + x)^s satisfies a Ramanujan-type identity generalizing Ramanujan's classical formula for ζ(2n+1). Specifically, the alternating Hurwitz kernel K_E^{2n+1}(α, x) := ½ζ_E(2n+1, x) + Σ_{m=1}^∞ m^{-2n-1}/(e^{2αm} + 1) obeys: α^{-n}·K_E^{2n+1}(α, x) − (−β)^{-n}·K_E^{2n+1}(β, 1−x) = 2^{2n} Σ_{k=0}^{n+1} (−1)^{k−1} E_{2k}(x) B_{2n−2k+2} / ((2k)!(2n−2k+2)!) · α^{n−k+1} β^k, where E_{2k}(x) are Euler polynomials and B_{2k} are Bernoulli numbers. This replaces the Bernoulli numbers B_{2k} in Ramanujan's original identity with Euler polynomials E_{2k}(x), reflecting the alternating (sign-twisted) structure.
proof_strategy: Adapt the classical proof of Ramanujan's identity via modular symmetry: (1) Define the alternating Hurwitz kernel K_E^s(α, x) and establish its meromorphic continuation using the contour integral representation of ζ_E(s, x); (2) Apply Poisson summation or Mellin transform techniques to derive the modular transformation α → π²/α on K_E, exploiting the functional symmetry x ↔ 1−x inherent to the alternating series; (3) Express the residues and poles of the transformed kernel in terms of Euler polynomials E_{2k}(x) via their generating function sech(t)·exp(xt) = Σ E_n(x) t^n/n!, matching the Bernoulli generating function t/(e^t−1) used in the classical proof; (4) Compare both sides as meromorphic functions of α, verifying equality at all poles and residues.
title: Alternating Hurwitz–Ramanujan Identity with Euler Polynomials

description: The paper proves that for k ≥ 3 and sufficiently large n, the maximum number of points in an n × n grid with no k+1 collinear points equals kn. This conjecture asserts that 'sufficiently large' can be replaced by the explicit threshold n ≥ k. Note that for n ≤ k the whole grid has no k+1 collinear points so f_k(n) = n², and for n = k we get f_k(k) = k² = k·k, making n ≥ k the natural boundary. The conjecture predicts that for all k ≥ 3 and n ≥ k, the trivial upper bound kn is always achievable.
proof_strategy: The paper's approach splits into: (1) handling 'heavy' lines via pseudorandom hypergraph matchings (Ehard-Glock-Joos), (2) crude deletion for remaining violations, (3) randomized switching to recover near-optimal size. To push 'sufficiently large n' down to n ≥ k, one would need to make each step effective with explicit bounds. The hypergraph matching step likely requires the most careful analysis for small n. A computer-verified case analysis for small n (up to some explicit bound) combined with the asymptotic argument for larger n could work. The key is determining whether the o(n) deletion/swinging losses can be controlled when n is close to k.
title: Explicit Threshold for No-(k+1)-in-line: f_k(n) = kn for all k ≥ 3 and n ≥ k

description: For every d ≥ 3, the supremum of normalized surface measures of zero-sum-free measurable subsets of the unit sphere S^{d-1} in ℝ^d equals exactly 1/2. Equivalently, every measurable zero-sum-free A ⊆ S^{d-1} satisfies σ_{d-1}(A) ≤ 1/2, with equality achieved (only) by open hemispheres. The paper establishes the asymptotic bound m_d ≤ 1/2 + O(1/d), but the exact value m_d = 1/2 remains open.
domain_bridges: Cap set problem and polynomial method (Croot-Lev-Pach / Ellenberg-Gijswijt)
Spherical harmonics and spectral analysis on S^{d-1}
proof_strategy: The paper establishes m_d ≤ ⌊(d+1)²/2⌋/(d(d+1)) = 1/2 + O(1/d) using spherical harmonics and a polynomial method argument. To prove the exact bound m_d = 1/2, one must close the O(1/d) gap. A potential strategy: (1) characterize the near-extremal sets more precisely using the spherical harmonic analysis already developed, (2) show that any set exceeding measure 1/2 + ε must have structural properties forcing it to contain a zero-sum triple, possibly by developing a spherical analogue of the slice-rank/polynomial method that yields exact rather than asymptotic bounds, or (3) establish a stability result showing near-hemisphere sets must be close to hemispheres, then use this rigidity to exclude the O(1/d) excess.
title: Bukh's Exact Zero-Sum-Free Density Conjecture

description: For a p-adic field F and a generic representation π of GL_r(F), the exterior square ε-factor defined via the Jacquet–Shalika local functional equation coincides with the exterior square ε-factor defined via the Langlands–Shahidi method: ε^{JS}(π, ∧², ψ) = ε^{Sh}(π, ∧², ψ). This is the main theorem (Theorem 1.1) of the paper. Formalizing it requires developing the theories of generic representations of GL_r over p-adic fields, both integral-representation (Jacquet–Shalika) and Langlands–Shahidi constructions of L- and ε-factors, and the local functional equation for the Jacquet–Shalika exterior square integrals.
proof_strategy: The original proof uses global methods: (1) construct a global automorphic representation whose local component at a designated p-adic place v is the given π, (2) exploit the equality of global ε-factors computed via both methods (using the global functional equation and the theory of global integrals), and (3) deduce the local equality by comparing local factors at all places, invoking the archimedean result of Jiang–Liu–Sun–Tian and the known equality ε^{Sh} = ε^{Gal} from Cogdell–Shahidi–Tsai. A formalization would need to first develop the local theories (Jacquet–Shalika integrals, Langlands–Shahidi L-functions, local ε-factors) and then formalize the globalization argument.
title: Equality of Jacquet–Shalika and Langlands–Shahidi exterior square ε-factors for GL_n over p-adic fields

description: For any natural numbers n, l, r such that n >= (l+1)*r + l, there exists an interval packing of maximum possible size (n choose l) in the Boolean lattice restricted to levels l through l+r. This can be formulated as the existence of a function f mapping each l-sized subset T of [n] to an r-sized subset C_T disjoint from T, such that for any distinct l-sized subsets T1, T2, T1 is not contained in T2 union C_T2 and T2 is not contained in T1 union C_T1.
proof_strategy: Define the explicit construction of the function f mapping each l-set T to an r-set C_T using the cyclic sequence method described in the paper. Subsequently, prove that the resulting intervals [T, T ∪ C_T] are pairwise disjoint by showing that for any two distinct l-sets T1, T2, neither T1 ⊆ T2 ∪ C_{T2} nor T2 ⊆ T1 ∪ C_{T1} holds.
title: Engel's Interval Packing Theorem

description: For any simple graph G with n vertices and m edges, and for any 1 ≤ k ≤ n-1, the sum of the k largest Laplacian eigenvalues s_k(G) equals m + binom(k+1, 2) if and only if G is a threshold graph with clique number k+1.
proof_strategy: Reduce the problem to the Grone-Merris-Bai theorem, which states s_k(G) ≤ ∑_{i=1}^k d_i^*(G) where d* is the conjugate degree sequence. Show that equality in Brouwer's bound implies equality in Grone-Merris-Bai, forcing the degree sequence to match the Laplacian eigenvalue sequence. Use the characterization of threshold graphs via their degree sequences and the specific sum m + binom(k+1, 2) to conclude that G must be a threshold graph with clique number k+1.
title: Full Brouwer's Laplacian Conjecture Equality Characterization

description: The number of lozenge tilings of the triangular region T_n equals the product over all 1 ≤ a < b ≤ 3n+2 with (a,b) ≠ (n+1,2n+2) of |1 + ζ^a + ζ^b|^(1/3), where ζ = exp(2πi/(3n+3)).
proof_strategy: Define the region T_n and its dual graph G_n. Define the bipartite adjacency matrix M_n of G_n. Prove that the number of perfect matchings of G_n equals the absolute value of the determinant of M_n. Diagonalize M_n to compute its determinant, and verify that the resulting expression matches the given product formula.
title: Exact Enumeration of Lozenge Tilings of Triangular Regions

description: The paper establishes that f(a,k) = Θ(a + k + ak/log(k+2)), where f(a,k) is the minimum degree threshold forcing k edge-disjoint Hamilton cycles in graphs with bipartite-hole number at most a. This conjecture proposes that the implicit constant in the upper bound can be taken to be 2, i.e., f(a,k) ≤ 2a + 2k + ⌈2ak / log(k+2)⌉ for all integers a,k ≥ 2. This would make the asymptotic result fully explicit and represents a natural strengthening of the paper's greedy-packing upper bound argument.
proof_strategy: Formalize the bipartite-hole deletion lemma and the McDiarmid-Yolov Hamiltonicity theorem as intermediate results, then construct the greedy packing argument with explicit bookkeeping of degree deficits at each stage. The key is tracking how the bipartite-hole number and minimum degree evolve after deleting each Hamilton cycle, showing the deficit is bounded by a factor of 2 times the target expression.
title: Explicit constant for bipartite-hole Hamilton cycle packing upper bound

description: The paper establishes a directed analogue of the Bonnet-Myers theorem: for a strongly connected, r-regular simple digraph G with in-curvature κ⁻(v) ≥ κ₀ > 0 at every vertex, the directed diameter is bounded above by 2r/κ₀. The natural rigidity conjecture is that equality in this bound forces G to be a directed cycle. Specifically, if G is a strongly connected, r-regular simple digraph with in-curvature κ⁻(v) ≥ κ₀ > 0 for all v, and the directed diameter satisfies ⟶diam(G) = 2r/κ₀, then G is isomorphic to a directed cycle C_n (where n = 2r/κ₀ + 1). This mirrors Obata's rigidity theorem for the classical Lichnerowicz inequality and would complete the directed Bonnet-Myers picture.
proof_strategy: Adapt Obata's rigidity argument from Riemannian geometry: (1) Formalize the directed Bonnet-Myers inequality from the paper in Lean, establishing the diameter bound. (2) Analyze the equality case by studying the structure of shortest directed paths achieving maximum distance. (3) Show that equality forces every vertex to lie on a unique longest directed geodesic, and that the out-neighborhood structure is rigid enough to force the directed cycle topology. (4) Use the permutation relation between in- and out-curvature (Theorem from the paper) to constrain the local structure at extremal vertices. (5) The key technical step is proving that any deviation from the directed cycle structure strictly increases the effective resistance / decreases curvature below κ₀, contradicting the equality assumption.
title: Directed Bonnet-Myers Rigidity: Equality Characterizes Directed Cycles

description: There exists a constant δ > 0 such that for every n ≥ 2, there exists a set P ⊂ ℝ² with |P| = n containing a distance occurring at least n^(1+δ) times. This is the core quantitative claim of the paper, establishing that the Minkowski grid construction yields a polynomial improvement over the trivial n bound for distance multiplicity, thereby disproving Erdős's unit distance conjecture.
proof_strategy: The proof requires constructing the Minkowski grid from a number field of high degree (vertical amplification of the Ramanujan estimate), showing the resulting point set has the claimed distance multiplicity. A Lean formalization would need: (1) the Croot-Mao-Pohoata-Sheffer-Yip robust Ramanujan lower bound for r_2(m), (2) the construction of the Minkowski grid P_n from an appropriate number field, (3) a counting argument bounding the maximum distance multiplicity from below by n^(1+δ). The number-theoretic ingredient about representations as sums of two squares in number fields is the key bridge.
title: Polynomially superlinear distance multiplicity in finite planar point sets

description: For every integer d ≥ 2, if p ∈ ℂ[s] is a nonzero balanced polynomial (satisfying p(s) = ω·conj(p(−conj(s))) for some |ω| = 1) whose zeros all lie in the region Ω_d = {a+ib : a² − b²/(d−1) ≤ d/4}, then the centered binomial sample B_d[p](z) = Σ_{j=0}^{d} C(d,j)·p(j−d/2)·z^j has all its zeros on the unit circle. Furthermore, Ω_d is the maximal reflection-invariant set with this property: for any reflection-invariant S ⊋ Ω_d, there exists a balanced polynomial with zeros in S whose binomial sample has a zero off the unit circle. This is the polynomial case of the paper's main sampling theorem, which then drives the derivative-period-polynomial unit-circle theorem for L-functions of newforms.
domain_bridges: Sampling theory → Zero distribution of L-functions
proof_strategy: Factor the balanced polynomial into reflected zero pairs {ρ, −ρ̄} and purely imaginary fixed zeros. Reduce to the single-pair case p_ρ(s) = (s−ρ)(s+ρ̄) via multiplicativity of the balanced condition under binomial sampling. For single pairs, apply projective Hermite–Kakeya–Obreschkoff theory to classify when B_d[p_ρ] has all zeros on 𝕋: the admissible region boundary is precisely the hyperbola a² − b²/(d−1) = d/4. De Bruijn strip contraction controls zero variation under parameter perturbation. Maximality follows from explicit counterexamples at boundary points of Ω_d.
title: Sharp Circular Sampling for Balanced Polynomials

description: For an elliptic curve E over Q with good supersingular reduction at 2 and square-free conductor, if the mu-invariant of its sharp/flat 2-adic L-function vanishes, then the lambda-invariant of the quadratic twist E^D (for square-free D > 0 with D ≡ 1 mod 4) differs from that of E by an explicit sum over the prime factors of D involving the 2-adic valuation of (ℓ^2 - 1)/8 and the parity of the number of points on E modulo ℓ.
proof_strategy: Decompose the variation of the sharp/flat 2-adic L-functions under quadratic twists by analyzing their interpolation properties and the local Euler factors at primes dividing D. Compare the resulting power series to deduce the difference in their Iwasawa invariants, adapting Matsuno's ordinary case methodology to the supersingular setting via Sprung's logarithmic matrices.
title: Supersingular Iwasawa Lambda Invariant Difference Formula

description: The paper proves that the count N(x) of odd integers up to x not representable as p+2^a+2^b is at least x * exp(-(4+η) * (logloglogx / loglogx) * logx). This conjecture posits that the constant 4 in the exponent is an artifact of the Fermat number construction and can be replaced by any arbitrarily small epsilon > 0, yielding a lower bound of x * exp(-ε * (logloglogx / loglogx) * logx). This would substantially bridge the gap to Erdős's grand challenge conjecture that N(x) > c_0 * x for some constant c_0 > 0.
proof_strategy: Improve the covering congruence system construction by replacing the reliance on Fermat numbers with a more general system of cyclotomic polynomials or finding a denser set of congruences that reduces the multiplicative constant penalty from 4 to an arbitrarily small epsilon.
title: Epsilon-Constant Reduction for Odd Integers Not of the Form p+2^a+2^b

catalog_references: Exact enumeration of lozenge tilings of a triangular region
description: The paper gives an exact product formula for the number of lozenge tilings T_n of a triangular region T_n involving complex roots of unity: T_n = ∏_{1≤a<b≤3n+2, (a,b)≠(n+1,2n+2)} |1+ζ^a+ζ^b|^{1/3} with ζ = e^{2πi/(3n+3)}. This conjecture states that this complicated product simplifies to a product of binomial coefficients: T_n = ∏_{k=1}^n (3k-1 choose k). This is a precise, falsifiable identity that can be checked for small n and would provide a much simpler closed form.
proof_strategy: The paper reduces T_n to the determinant of a bipartite adjacency matrix M_n and diagonalizes it. The eigenvalues are the factors |1+ζ^a+ζ^b|. One could attempt to simplify the product of these eigenvalues using trigonometric identities and known product formulas for binomial coefficients. Alternatively, compute T_n for small n to guess the recurrence, then prove the recurrence holds for the binomial product and matches the determinant formula via creative telescoping or the holonomic systems approach.
title: Simplified binomial product formula for lozenge tilings of the triangular region T_n

description: The infimum μ₂ over all infinite sequences of radial cuts of the ratio between the maximum and minimum portion (adjacent pair of slices) sizes equals 1+ρ, where ρ is the unique real root of ρ²+ρ³=1 in (0,1). The paper proves μ₂ ≤ 1+ρ ≈ 1.75488 and Korsky proved μ₂ ≥ 5/3 ≈ 1.66667, but the exact value remains open.
proof_strategy: The upper bound μ₂ ≤ 1+ρ follows from the paper's construction and Proposition 1 on cyclic factor avoidance. The lower bound μ₂ ≥ 1+ρ requires showing that no infinite sequence of cuts can achieve a ratio strictly less than 1+ρ. This likely requires analyzing the combinatorial constraints on infinite words over the alphabet {0,1,2,3} with ratios 1:ρ:ρ²:ρ³, proving that any such word avoiding equal adjacent letters must contain a portion with ratio at least (1+ρ)/(ρ²+ρ³) = 1+ρ. A potential approach uses the substitution system properties: the map sending 0↦23 (or 32), 1↦0, 2↦1, 3↦2 shows that any valid infinite sequence must eventually approximate the fixed point, forcing portions near the extremal ratio.
title: Optimality of the cake-cutting constant μ₂

description: For a complete multipartite graph G = K_{n_1,...,n_m} with n_1 ≤ ... ≤ n_m, the path-free complex PF_t(G) is vertex decomposable if and only if t ≥ 2n_{m-1} - 1. Equivalently, this is exactly the range where PF_t(G) is shellable and sequentially Cohen-Macaulay. For t ≤ 2n_{m-1} - 2, the complex fails to be sequentially Cohen-Macaulay.
proof_strategy: Formalize simplicial complexes and vertex decomposability in Lean, then define PF_t(G) as the simplicial complex of vertex subsets with no induced P_t. Define complete multipartite graphs and their part-size ordering. The forward direction (t ≥ 2n_{m-1}-1 ⟹ vertex decomposable) requires formalizing the explicit structural decomposition of PF_t(G) as a union of join complexes with a size-truncation term, then proving each join component is vertex decomposable and that the union preserves this property. The reverse direction (t ≤ 2n_{m-1}-2 ⟹ not sequentially Cohen-Macaulay) requires constructing a specific non-Cohen-Macaulay witness face or showing the homology fails the sequential Cohen-Macaulay condition, potentially via a Mayer-Vietoris spectral sequence argument.
title: Vertex decomposability threshold for path-free complexes of complete multipartite graphs

description: The number of length-n quasinecklaces Q_k(n) is exactly k times the number of length-n necklaces N_k(n) for all k ≥ 2 and n ≥ 1.
proof_strategy: Demonstrate that each necklace corresponds to exactly k quasinecklaces via rotational symmetry or quasinecklace construction rules.
title: Proportionality of quasinecklaces to necklaces

description: For every doubly regular tournament T on n vertices (where n ≡ 3 mod 4, n ≥ 3), the metric dimension β(T) ≤ 2⌈log₂ n⌉. This extends the paper's O(log n) bound proven for certain doubly regular team tournaments to the classical and well-studied family of doubly regular tournaments, which are regular tournaments with parameters (n, (n-1)/2, (n-3)/4). The conjecture posits an explicit constant of 2, making it directly falsifiable by computing metric dimensions of small doubly regular tournaments (n = 3, 7, 11, 19, ...) and checking against the bound.
proof_strategy: Adapt Babai's probabilistic method as used in the paper: for a doubly regular tournament T, randomly sample k = 2⌈log₂ n⌉ vertices as a resolving set candidate. Compute the probability that two distinct vertices u, v receive the same distance vector from the sampled set. Use the strong regularity properties of doubly regular tournaments—specifically that every pair of vertices has exactly (n-3)/4 common out-neighbours—to bound the collision probability per pair by 1/2^k. Apply a union bound over all n(n-1)/2 pairs, choosing k so that the union bound is < 1, yielding a resolving set of size at most 2⌈log₂ n⌉.
title: Logarithmic metric dimension of doubly regular tournaments

description: The paper proves that for $k \ge 3$ and sufficiently large $n$, the maximum size of a subset of the $n \times n$ grid with no $k+1$ collinear points is exactly $kn$. This conjecture posits that the condition 'sufficiently large $n$' can be relaxed to $n > k$, meaning $f_k(n) = kn$ holds for all $k \ge 3$ and $n > k$. This would unify the trivial case ($n \le k$, where $f_k(n) = n^2$) and the asymptotic regime.
proof_strategy: Either refine the probabilistic and pseudorandom hypergraph matching arguments to explicitly compute the threshold $N(k)$ and show it is $k+1$, or find a constructive algebraic or combinatorial proof that works uniformly for all $n > k$.
title: Exact Threshold for No-$(k+1)$-in-line Problem

description: The constant μ₂ is defined as the infimum over all infinite sequences of radial cuts of a unit circular cake of the supremum over n of the ratio (maximum portion size)/(minimum portion size) after n cuts, where a portion is an adjacent pair of slices. The paper proves μ₂ ≤ 1 + ρ where ρ ≈ 0.75488 is the unique real root of ρ² + ρ³ = 1. The conjecture asserts this bound is tight: μ₂ = 1 + ρ, meaning no cutting strategy can achieve a worst-case portion ratio strictly below 1 + ρ. This would also establish μ₂ as irrational, since ρ is irrational.
proof_strategy: The upper bound μ₂ ≤ 1 + ρ is proven constructively via a specific cutting algorithm and a word-avoidance argument over {0,1,2,3}. The lower bound μ₂ ≥ 1 + ρ remains wide open (only μ₂ ≥ 5/3 is known). A plausible approach: (1) Show that any infinite cutting sequence achieving ratio < 1 + ρ must, after sufficient normalization, produce slices whose sizes lie in ratios from {1, ρ, ρ², ρ³}, (2) Prove that the corresponding word over {0,1,2,3} must avoid all factors in the forbidden set A from Proposition O, (3) Show by combinatorial or automata-theoretic means that no infinite word cyclically avoiding A can have all adjacent-pair sums below 1 + ρ times the minimum adjacent-pair sum. Alternatively, a potential-function argument tracking the distribution of slice sizes could force a lower bound.
title: The optimal portion ratio μ₂ equals 1 + ρ
