description: For a complete multipartite graph $K_{n_1, \dots, n_m}$ with $n_1 \le \dots \le n_m$ and $m \ge 2$, the $t$-path-free complex $\PF_t(K_{n_1, \dots, n_m})$ is vertex decomposable if and only if $t \ge 2n_{m-1} - 1$.
proof_strategy: First formalize abstract simplicial complexes, the $t$-path-free complex $\PF_t(G)$, and vertex decomposability in Lean. Then, formalize the structural decomposition of $\PF_t(G)$ as a union of join complexes. Establish that for $t \le 2n_{m-1} - 2$, the complex fails to be sequentially Cohen-Macaulay by analyzing the link of a specific face. Finally, prove vertex decomposability for $t \ge 2n_{m-1} - 1$ by explicitly constructing the shedding vertex sequence and applying the decomposition theorem.
title: Vertex Decomposability of Path-Free Complexes of Complete Multipartite Graphs

catalog_references: Ciucu, A. & Krattenthaler, P. (2002). Lozenge tilings of a triangular region. arXiv:math/0206123.
Propp, J. (2002). The many faces of alternating-sign matrices. SIAM Review, 44(2), 323–343.
Kasteleyn, P. W. (1961). Graphs and simple pairwise interactions. Physica, 27, 1209‑1223.
Temperley, H. N. V., & Fisher, M. E. (1961). Dimer problem in statistical mechanics‑an exact result. Philosophical Magazine, 6(68), 1061‑1062.
MacMahon, A. M. (1978). Plane partitions. In Combinatorial Mathematics (pp. 199‑212). Springer.
description: We conjecture that for every positive integer n, the signed adjacency matrix M_n of the dual graph of the triangular region T_n has eigenvalues exactly π_k = 2 cos(π k/(3n+3)) for k = 1,2,…,3n+2, excluding k = n+1 and k = 2n+2. Consequently, the determinant of M_n (which counts lozenge tilings) equals the product ∏_{k∈S_n} π_k, matching the product formula proved in the paper.
proof_strategy: Apply discrete Fourier transform on the cyclic group ℤ_{3n+3} to diagonalize M_n. The eigenvectors are given by characters χ_j(v) = ζ^{jv} where ζ = e^{2πi/(3n+3)}. Computing M_n·χ_j yields eigenvalue π_j = ζ^a + ζ^b + ζ^{-a-b} for appropriate a,b, which simplifies to 2 cos(π j/(3n+3)). The exceptional pair (n+1,2n+2) corresponds to a zero eigenvalue, which is omitted from the spectrum. Hence the eigenvalues are exactly the claimed cosines, and the determinant matches the product formula.
title: Eigenvalue conjecture for the signed adjacency matrix M_n of the triangular region's dual graph

description: There exists a constant δ > 0 such that for every integer n ≥ 2, there exists a finite set P ⊂ ℝ² of n points where the most frequent nonzero distance occurs at least n^(1+δ) times among ordered pairs. This is the core quantitative claim of the paper: the Minkowski grid construction vertically amplifies the one-dimensional Ramanujan estimate for r₂ to produce point sets whose distance multiplicity is superlinear, thereby yielding counterexamples to Erdős's unit distance conjecture under scaling.
proof_strategy: Construct P as a Minkowski grid over a number field K/ℚ of degree d ≥ 2. Points lie in a scaled lattice derived from the ring of integers of K, so that squared distances correspond to values of the norm form N_{K/ℚ}. The Ramanujan estimate max_{m≤x} r_d(m) ≥ exp(c·log x / log log x) for the number of representations by the norm form, combined with the vertical amplification from dimension 1 to 2, yields the exponent gain δ = δ(d) > 0. The parameter δ arises from the interplay between the degree d and the pigeonhole-type averaging over the grid.
title: Superlinear distance multiplicity in Minkowski grids

description: The paper proves that μ₂ ≤ 1 + ρ, where μ₂ is the infimum over all infinite sequences of radial cuts of the supremum of the ratio of maximum to minimum portion (adjacent-pair) sizes, and ρ ≈ 0.75488 is the unique real root of x² + x³ = 1 in (0,1). Korsky proved μ₂ ≥ 5/3. The conjecture asserts that the paper's upper bound is tight: μ₂ = 1 + ρ. This would require showing that no cutting strategy can achieve a ratio strictly less than 1 + ρ in the limit, which likely demands a structural impossibility argument about the combinatorics of slice-size configurations.
proof_strategy: To prove μ₂ ≥ 1 + ρ, one must show that for any infinite cutting strategy and any ε > 0, there exists some n such that the ratio of maximum to minimum portion size after n cuts is at least 1 + ρ - ε. A possible approach: (1) characterize the set of achievable slice-size configurations as words over a finite alphabet of size classes, (2) show via a combinatorial/entropy argument that any long word avoiding the forbidden patterns from Proposition 2 must contain a factor whose portion ratio approaches 1 + ρ, or (3) use a potential function argument showing that any deviation from the ρ² : ρ³ splitting rule inevitably creates worse imbalances.
title: Tightness of the adjacent-pair cake-cutting bound: μ₂ = 1 + ρ

description: Erdős repeatedly asked whether there exists an absolute constant c_0 > 0 such that for all sufficiently large x, the number N(x) of odd integers n ≤ x which cannot be written as p + 2^a + 2^b (with p a prime and a, b natural numbers) satisfies N(x) > c_0 * x. This asserts that a positive proportion of odd integers are not of this form, upgrading the current x^{1-o(1)} lower bounds to a positive density.
proof_strategy: Establish that the set of odd integers not representable in this form has positive lower asymptotic density. This likely requires bypassing the exponential bounds produced by covering congruence systems, perhaps by demonstrating that a positive proportion of integers fall into residue classes that are fundamentally excluded by the structure of cyclotomic prime divisors, or by applying additive combinatorics to bound the density of the sumset.
title: Positive Lower Asymptotic Density of Odd Integers Not Representable as p + 2^a + 2^b

description: For every primitive holomorphic newform f of weight k ≥ 4, level N, and nebentypus χ, and for every non-negative integer m, all zeros of the derivative period polynomial P⁽ᵐ⁾_f(z) = Σ_{j=0}^{k-2} C(k-2,j) · Λ⁽ᵐ⁾(f, j+1) · z^j lie on the unit circle, where Λ(f,s) denotes the completed L-function. This confirms and extends the Diamantis–Rolen conjecture to arbitrary level, nebentypus, and derivative order. The core mechanism is a sharp circular sampling theorem: for balanced polynomials p with zeros in Ω_d = {a+ib : a² − b²/(d−1) ≤ d/4}, the centered binomial sample B_d[p] has all zeros on the unit circle.
proof_strategy: Stage 1: Formalize the sharp circular sampling theorem for balanced polynomials — if p is balanced (p = ω·J(p) with |ω|=1, where J(F)(s) = conj(F(-conj(s)))) and Z(p) ⊆ Ω_{d,δ}, then all zeros of B_{d,δ}[p](z) = Σ C(d,j)·p(δ(j−d/2))·z^j lie on the unit circle, with Ω_{d,δ} maximal. Stage 2: Build completed L-function infrastructure for primitive holomorphic newforms, establishing the functional equation (supplying the balancing symmetry) and the Euler-product zero-free half-plane (placing reflected zeros in the required strip). Stage 3: Apply the sampling theorem with de Bruijn strip contraction and projective HKO theory to transport completed-zero geometry to derivative period polynomial circularity, simplicity, and strict interlacing.
title: Derivative Period Polynomial Unit-Circle Theorem for Primitive Holomorphic Newforms

description: For every elliptic curve E/Q with good supersingular reduction at 2 and square-free conductor, the sharp and flat μ-invariants of Sprung's 2-adic L-functions vanish: μ₂^♯(E,ωⁱ) = μ₂^♭(E,ωⁱ) = 0 for all i ∈ {0,1}. This is a 2-adic supersingular analogue of Greenberg's μ=0 conjecture. Its truth would render the λ-invariant difference formula in the paper unconditional, extending Matsuno-type formulas completely to the supersingular setting at p=2.
proof_strategy: Establish the vanishing of algebraic μ-invariants for the signed (♯/♭) Selmer groups via control theorems and the structure of torsion in Mordell–Weil groups over the cyclotomic Z₂-extension. Then invoke the Iwasawa main conjecture for supersingular primes (proved by Kobayashi, Sprung, etc.) to transfer vanishing from the algebraic to the analytic side. The supersingular condition at 2, combined with square-free conductor, constrains the 2-adic torsion structure sufficiently to force μ=0.
title: Vanishing of sharp/flat 2-adic μ-invariants for semistable supersingular elliptic curves

description: The supremum of achievable vertical amplification parameters δ in the paper's main theorem equals 1/3. Precisely: for every ε > 0, there exist infinitely many n ∈ ℕ and finite sets P ⊂ ℝ² with |P| = n such that for every A ⊆ P with |A| ≥ 2, the maximum distance multiplicity μ(A) ≥ |A|² / n^(2/3 + ε). This would be optimal given the O(n^{4/3}) Szemerédi–Trotter upper bound on unit distances, which forces δ ≤ 1/3. The paper establishes existence of some δ > 0; this conjectures δ can approach 1/3 via increasingly high-degree number field constructions.
proof_strategy: Extend the vertical amplification technique using number fields of degree d → ∞, combining the robust Ramanujan-type estimates from Croot-Mao-Pohoata-Sheffer-Yip with Minkowski lattice constructions from number fields with rich representations of integers as sums of squares. The key is to show that as the degree d grows, the amplification factor δ_d approaches 1/3, matching the Szemerédi–Trotter barrier. A potential approach involves cyclotomic fields or more general number fields where the class number and unit structure provide increasingly many representations.
title: Optimal Vertical Amplification Conjecture for Planar Point Sets

description: For any fixed integer $r \ge 2$ and $\varepsilon > 0$, every sufficiently large finite uncrowded $(r+1)$-uniform hypergraph of maximum degree $\Delta$ has list chromatic number at most $(1+\varepsilon)(r\Delta/\log\Delta)^{1/r}$. This captures the paper's main theorem, improving the leading constant from $r$ to $r^{1/r}$ over prior work by Iliopoulos.
proof_strategy: Formalize the semi-random list-coloring nibble method directly on the hypergraph, defining active edge-color constraints to track residual sizes. Establish a binomial degree bound to maintain invariants during the nibble phase, then apply a Rosenfeld-style counting argument to complete the coloring in the sparse terminal state.
title: Asymptotic List Chromatic Number of Uncrowded Uniform Hypergraphs

description: Conjecture: Let ρ be the unique real root of x^2 + x^3 = 1 in (0,1). Define μ₂ as the infimum over all infinite sequences of radial cuts of a circular cake (as described in the paper) of the supremum over time of the ratio between the largest and smallest portion (adjacent pair of slices). Then μ₂ = 1+ρ.
proof_strategy: To prove the conjecture, one would first establish the known upper bound μ₂ ≤ 1+ρ by exhibiting the specific cutting process given in the paper. For the lower bound μ₂ ≥ 1+ρ, one would analyze the combinatorial constraints on slice sizes imposed by the cutting rule and show that any infinite sequence must eventually produce a portion whose size ratio is at least 1+ρ. This can be approached by modeling the slice sizes as a multiplicative walk on the set {1, ρ, ρ², ρ³} and using a potential function or invariant derived from the forbidden factors in Proposition~O\\ref{propNoRepeat} to bound the frequency of large slices relative to small ones, ultimately yielding the desired ratio.
title: Optimality of the 1+ρ bound for the maximum-to-minimum portion ratio in the iterative cake-cutting process

description: The partial dominating set value function |N[S]| (number of vertices dominated by a set S) cannot be expressed as an FO Value expression with quantifier-free correction terms over the vocabulary of graphs. Concretely: for every unary weight function w : V(G) → ℕ and every quantifier-free formula φ(x₁,...,xₘ) over the vocabulary {E}, there exists a graph G and a finite set S ⊆ V(G) such that |N_G[S]| ≠ (Σ_{v ∈ S} w(v)) − |{(v₁,...,vₘ) ∈ Sᵐ : G ⊨ φ(v₁,...,vₘ)}|. This contrasts with Partial Vertex Cover, which the paper shows is a quantifier-free FO Value instance via the identity |{e : e ∩ S ≠ ∅}| = Σ_{v ∈ S} deg(v) − |E(G[S])|, where the correction term E(x,y) is quantifier-free. The dominating set value requires counting vertices outside S that are adjacent to multiple vertices in S, necessitating existential quantification over vertices not in the selected tuple.
proof_strategy: Construct a family of graphs G_k parameterized by k such that for any quantifier-free formula φ with m free variables and any unary weight w, one can find a set S in some G_k where the quantifier-free FO Value decomposition fails. The key insight is that quantifier-free formulas over the tuple variables can only detect local adjacency patterns among selected vertices, but |N[S]| depends on the number of external vertices adjacent to multiple tuple elements—a global property requiring existential quantification over vertices outside S. A candidate proof uses Hanf-locality of quantifier-free FO: two tuples with the same atomic type in G yield the same correction value, but can dominate different numbers of external vertices, breaking the decomposition.
title: Inexpressibility of Partial Dominating Set as Quantifier-Free FO Value

description: For every integer k ≥ 3, there exists a constant c_k > 0 such that every C_{2k}-free graph with average degree at least c_k · h contains an induced subdivision of K_h. This conjectures that the polylogarithmic factor in the authors' bound of Ω_k(h log^5 h) can be eliminated, making the threshold purely linear in h, which would be tight up to the constant factor.
proof_strategy: Refine the embedding techniques from the paper to eliminate the logarithmic factors introduced during iterative path-finding and pseudorandomness exploitation. Key insight: C_{2k}-free graphs have stronger pseudo-random properties than currently exploited, and more careful use of the dependent random choice or balanced-supergraph techniques could yield path systems that directly give induced subdivisions without the logarithmic overhead from iterative refinement.
title: Linear threshold for induced clique subdivisions in even-cycle-free graphs

description: For P(X) = X² + 1, the number of pairs (n, m) with 1 ≤ n < m ≤ N such that (n²+1)(m²+1) is a perfect square is O(logᴬ N) for some absolute constant A ≥ 0. This is equivalent to the variance of the extended Rademacher partial sum ∑_{n≤N} f(n²+1) satisfying Var = N + O(logᴬ N), meaning the off-diagonal contribution is negligible. The equation (n²+1)(m²+1) = k² reduces via Gaussian integer norms to the Pythagorean-type condition (nm−1)² + (n+m)² = k², which for fixed n yields Pell equations whose solutions grow exponentially, giving only O(log N) solutions per n. The conjecture asserts the total across all n ≤ N remains polylogarithmic.
proof_strategy: For each fixed n, factor n²+1 and analyze the generalized Pell equation (n²+1)(m²+1) = k². Use the structure of solutions to Pell equations parametrized by fundamental units in Q(√(−(n²+1))) and related fields. The key is to show that for each n, the number of m ≤ N with (n²+1)(m²+1) = □ is O(log N), and then sum over n using that n²+1 has few representations as norms from quadratic extensions. The Gaussian integer factorization (n²+1)(m²+1) = |(n+i)(m+i)|² = |(nm−1)+(n+m)i|² transforms the problem into counting Pythagorean representations, where height bounds on rational points control the count.
title: Polylogarithmic Paucity of Square Products of Shifted Squares

description: For any ε > 0, there exist effectively computable constants C(ε) > 0 and Q₀(ε) > 0 such that: if for every primitive quadratic Dirichlet character χ with conductor q ≥ Q₀(ε), all non-real zeros ρ of L(s,χ) satisfy Re(ρ) ≤ 1 - C(ε)/log(q), then there is at most one such character χ whose associated L-function has a real zero β in the interval [1 - q^(-ε), 1). This formalizes the paper's main result that excluding non-real zeros from a shrinking neighborhood of s=1 allows a significant refinement of Page's theorem.
proof_strategy: The proof requires establishing: (1) effective zero-free regions for Dirichlet L-functions excluding the Landau-Siegel possibility; (2) a translation mechanism from lower bounds on L(1,χ) to upper bounds on exceptional real zeros β; (3) a counting argument showing that the hypothesis on non-real zeros (lying outside σ ≥ 1 - C/log(q)) prevents the distortion that would allow multiple exceptional characters. Key ingredients include logarithmic derivative estimates for L-functions, the Deuring-Heilbronn phenomenon, and effective bounds from the geometry of the zeros. Formalization would proceed by first establishing the effective constants, then the conditional zero-free region, and finally the uniqueness of the exceptional zero.
title: Conditional Refinement of Page's Theorem on Landau-Siegel Zeros

description: For the free Catalan structure (C, e, λ, ⊕) satisfying the unique decomposition property from Definition 1, the involution h = rev ∘ corev ∘ rev restricted to level C_n has exactly C_n fixed points, where C_n = (2n choose n)/(n+1) is the n-th Catalan number. This asserts that the fixed-point enumerator of h matches the Catalan generating function.
proof_strategy: First inductively define the free Catalan structure as an inductive type mirroring the three-form decomposition (empty | λ(s) | λ(u) ⊕ v with v ≠ e). Define rev and corev by structural recursion on the first-return and last-return decompositions respectively. Prove h = rev ∘ corev ∘ rev is involutive. Then establish the fixed-point count by constructing an explicit bijection between Fix(h|_{C_n}) and binary trees on n internal nodes, using the characterization that t is a fixed point iff rev(t) = corev(t).
title: Fixed points of involution h on the free Catalan structure are counted by Catalan numbers

description: An extension of the Colorful Carathéodory theorem to convex cones: given $r \ge d$ pairwise disjoint sets of vectors in $\mathbb{R}^d$ such that the origin is in the convex cone generated by each set, there exists a colorful transversal whose convex cone also contains the origin.
proof_strategy: Translate the topological proof into Lean by establishing that the support complexes of oriented matroids are near-$(d-1)$-Leray, and then applying a homological vanishing argument to deduce the existence of the colorful transversal in the cone setting.
title: Cone Colorful Carathéodory Theorem

description: Every exotic Diophantine triple {a, b, c} of distinct nonzero polynomials in ℝ[X] with at least one nonconstant element must contain the element 1. That is, if a+1, b+1, c+1, ab+1, ac+1, bc+1, and abc+1 are all perfect squares in ℝ[X], and at least one of a, b, c is nonconstant, then one of a, b, c equals 1.
domain_bridges: polynomial arithmetic over real closed fields
proof_strategy: Formalize the Filipin-Jurasić regularity theorem for polynomial Diophantine quadruples over ℝ[X], which classifies the structure of such quadruples. Then show that any exotic triple {a, b, c} (equivalently, a Diophantine quadruple {1, a, b, c} with abc+1 a square) with a nonconstant element and no element equal to 1 leads to a contradiction with this regularity structure.
title: Exotic Diophantine triples in ℝ[X] must contain 1

description: For any prime p, any p-adic optimization ℓ: ℚ_p^n → ℝ_{≥0} ∪ {∞}, any E ∈ ℕ, and any finite set C ⊆ (ℤ/p^Eℤ)^n, if (1) for all c ∈ dom(ℓ) \ π_E^{-1}(C) there exists d ∈ C with ℓ(d) < ℓ(c), and (2) for all c ∈ π_E^{-1}(C), ℓ(π_E(c)) ≤ ℓ(c), then ℓ is (E,C)-reducible: every optimal solution of OP(ℓ,C) is optimal for OP(ℓ), and every optimal solution c of OP(ℓ) satisfies c ∈ π_E^{-1}(C) with π_E(c) optimal for OP(ℓ,C). This is the key structural proposition enabling the generalized Baker forcing method.
proof_strategy: Direct verification from definitions. Condition (1) forces any global optimum into π_E^{-1}(C); condition (2) ensures the projected point achieves the same objective value, yielding both conditions of (E,C)-reducibility. Formalization requires: (a) defining ℚ_p and the projection π_E: ℚ_p^n → (ℤ/p^Eℤ)^n, (b) defining p-adic optimizations as partial maps ℚ_p^n → ℝ_{≥0} ∪ {∞}, (c) defining (E,C)-reducibility and the restricted optimization problem OP(ℓ,C), then proving the two optimality conditions follow from the hypotheses.
title: Optimality Restriction Lemma for (E,C)-Reducibility of p-adic Optimizations

description: For any integer $k \ge 4$, there exists a constant $C_k > 0$ such that for all positive integers $N$, the minimum modulus of a non-vanishing sum of $k$ $N$-th roots of unity satisfies $f(k, N) \le C_k \cdot N^{-k/4}$. This would generalize Myerson's asymptotic bound $f(k,N) \le N^{-k/4+o_N(1)}$ for even $k$ and even $N$ to all $k \ge 4$ and all $N$, vastly improving upon the logarithmic growth of the exponent $\alpha_k$ established in the paper.
proof_strategy: Extend the perturbation method of Barber and the author using inhomogeneous Diophantine approximation to systematically construct cancellations achieving order $N^{-k/4}$ for arbitrary $k$ and $N$, bypassing the parity constraints of Myerson's original construction.
title: Linear Exponent Conjecture for Small Sums of Roots of Unity

description: For every Turán graph T(n, r) with r ≥ 4 and n ≥ 4r, and for every edge e of T(n, r), the Seidel energy strictly increases upon deletion: E_S(T(n, r) − e) > E_S(T(n, r)). This is Theorem 1.2 of the paper, resolving a problem of Tian et al., but its formalization requires building the entire theory of Seidel matrices, Seidel energy, Turán graphs, and the reduced-order spectral machinery for blow-up graphs—a substantial formalization undertaking.
proof_strategy: First formalize Seidel matrices and Seidel energy in Lean, then define Turán graphs and independent-set blow-up graphs. Establish the reduced-order spectral criterion that reduces the Seidel energy comparison to eigenvalue analysis of a smaller matrix whose order depends only on the number of partite sets. Apply this criterion to the Turán graph case with r ≥ 4 and n ≥ 4r, verifying the inequality via explicit eigenvalue computation on the reduced matrix.
title: Seidel energy strictly increases under edge deletion in Turán graphs

catalog_references: Induced matching numbers in dense graphs
description: We conjecture that for the critical case ε=1/2, the maximal anti-Ramsey function for P_4 admits an exact quadratic lower bound with a computable constant. Specifically, we propose that χ_S(n, (n choose 2) - ⌊n^{3/2}⌋, P_4) > (1/8 - o(1))·n² as n → ∞, where the constant 1/8 arises from the induced matching structure in graphs with minimum degree (1/2 + o(1))n. This conjecture addresses the sharpness of the phase transition at ε=1/2 and would require establishing both the lower bound and matching upper bound to determine the exact asymptotic behavior.
domain_bridges: Connections between induced matchings and rainbow colorings
Relationship to the Erdős-Gallai theorem on paths
Bridge between extremal graph theory and Ramsey-type colorings
Threshold phenomena in sparse-dense graph transitions
proof_strategy: The proof would require three main components: (1) Constructive lower bound via explicit graph families showing χ_S(n, (n choose 2) - ⌊n^{3/2}⌋, P_4) ≥ (1/8 - o(1))·n² using induced matching analysis; (2) Upper bound construction demonstrating that no more than (1/8 + o(1))·n² colors are needed; (3) Stability analysis around the minimum degree threshold (1/2)n to verify the exact constant. The approach involves analyzing the structure of graphs missing Θ(n^{3/2}) edges and their P_4 rainbow colorings through induced matching decompositions.
title: Sharp Threshold and Exact Constant for P_4 Anti-Ramsey Number at ε=1/2

description: The Kaneko-Zagier conjecture posits that there exists a well-defined ring isomorphism between the quotient ring of multiple zeta values Z / zeta(2)Z and the ring of finite multiple zeta values Z_A. Specifically, the map sending a symmetric multiple zeta value zeta_S(k) to its corresponding finite multiple zeta value zeta_A(k) is well-defined and preserves the algebraic structures, meaning any Q-linear relation among SMZVs corresponds to an identical relation among FMZVs.
proof_strategy: Define the algebras of MZVs, SMZVs, and FMZVs in Lean. Establish the stuffle and shuffle relations for both SMZVs and FMZVs. Prove that the kernel of the natural projection from MZVs to SMZVs is generated by zeta(2), and show that the map sending SMZVs to FMZVs respects all algebraic relations, thereby establishing the ring isomorphism.
title: Kaneko-Zagier Conjecture for Symmetric and Finite MZVs

description: For the odd Euler ensemble at cutoff N, the positive spectral moments M^{odd}_{s,+}(N; n) satisfy the precise limit: lim_{N → ∞} √(2N/π) · M^{odd}_{s,+}(N; n) / |n|^s = ζ(s) for all real s > 1 and nonzero integers n. This identifies the Riemann zeta function as the spectral moment generating function emerging from the continuum limit of the marginally stable turbulent attractor, bridging the arithmetic structure of reduced rational angles p/q with the Lyapunov stability analysis of incompressible Navier–Stokes turbulence.
proof_strategy: Formalize the finite-N spectral problem over reduced rationals p/q and winding sectors r, establish the parity constraint N - qr ≡ 0 (mod 2) ruling out r = 0 for odd N, then apply coprime cotangent sum asymptotics and Jordan totient identities to derive the moment limit. The key step is expressing M^{odd}_{s,+}(N; n) as a sum over coprime pairs (p, q) with q odd, weighted by |n/q|^s, and showing the normalization √(2N/π) converts the discrete sum to ζ(s) via Euler product or Dirichlet series techniques available in Mathlib's number theory layer.
title: Odd Euler Ensemble Spectral Moment Zeta Convergence

catalog_references: Bonnet, Kim, Thomassé, Watrigant - Twin-width I (arXiv:2007.04352)
Bonnet, Geniet, Tessera, Thomassé - Twin-width VII (arXiv:2202.07006, QI invariance of twin-width)
Gromov - Groups of polynomial growth and expanding maps (1981)
Wilkes - Finitely generated inaccessible residually p-finite groups (2019)
description: Every finitely generated virtually nilpotent group has finite twin-width. This conjecture provides a positive structural guarantee for the combinatorial parameter of twin-width from the algebraic assumption of virtual nilpotence, complementing the paper's negative result that finite twin-width does not imply accessibility. Specifically, if Γ is a finitely generated group containing a nilpotent subgroup of finite index, then every Cayley graph of Γ has finite twin-width (i.e., the supremum of twin-widths of finite induced subgraphs is bounded). The proof would proceed by: (1) establishing that Z^n has finite twin-width by bounding the twin-width of subgraphs of the n-dimensional grid, (2) showing that torsion-free finitely generated nilpotent groups embed as discrete cocompact subgroups of nilpotent Lie groups, yielding quasi-isometric embeddings into R^m whose integer lattice Z^m has finite twin-width, and (3) applying the quasi-isometric invariance of twin-width for bounded-degree graphs (Twin-width VII, Bonnet et al.) together with finite-index arguments for the virtual case.
domain_bridges: Nilpotent group structure theory ↔ grid graph twin-width bounds
Quasi-isometric invariance of twin-width ↔ geometric group theory invariants
Cayley graph combinatorics ↔ Lie group embedding theorems (Mal'cev)
proof_strategy: Step 1: Prove the n-dimensional integer grid Z^n (as a Cayley graph with standard generators) has twin-width at most n+1, by constructing explicit contraction sequences for finite grid subgraphs that maintain bounded red degree. Step 2: Show that every torsion-free finitely generated nilpotent group N admits a discrete cocompact embedding into its Mal'cev completion (a simply-connected nilpotent Lie group), so that N is quasi-isometric to R^m equipped with a nilpotent Lie group metric, and hence N is quasi-isometric to a finite-index subgroup of Z^m (via the integer lattice). Step 3: Apply the quasi-isometric invariance of finite twin-width for bounded-degree graphs (Twin-width VII) to conclude that N has finite twin-width. Step 4: Extend to virtually nilpotent groups: if G has a nilpotent subgroup H of finite index, then G is quasi-isometric to H, and since H has finite twin-width by Step 3, so does G.
title: Finite Twin-Width of Virtually Nilpotent Groups

description: For an elliptic curve E over Q with good supersingular reduction at 2 and square-free D ≡1 mod 4, the difference in sharp/flat λ-invariants under quadratic twist by D should include a term proportional to the μ-invariant when μ ≠ 0.
proof_strategy: Extend the existing formula by analyzing the μ-invariant's contribution through local-global principles and modular forms.
title: Extension of Matsuno's Formula for Non-Vanishing μ-Invariants

description: Conjecture that the number Q_k(n) of length‑n quasinecklaces over a k‑letter alphabet equals the classical count of primitive words, i.e. ℑ Q_k(n) = π_{d|n} μ(d) k^{n/d} for all integers k ≥ 2 and n ≥ 1.
proof_strategy: We would prove the conjecture by establishing a bijection between quasinecklaces and primitive words, or by showing that the recurrence defining quasinecklaces derived in the paper matches the Möbius inversion of the total word count. A proof by induction on n using divisor decomposition and properties of the Möbius function can be formalized in Lean, leveraging existing libraries for arithmetic functions and finite sums.
title: Exact formula for the number of quasinecklaces

description: For integers n, k, ℓ with n > 100·ℓ·k² and 3 ≤ ℓ < k, if F ⊆ ([n] choose k) and G ⊆ ([n] choose ℓ) are non-trivial cross-intersecting families (i.e., ⋂_{F∈F} F = ∅ and ⋂_{G∈G} G = ∅, and F ∩ G ≠ ∅ for all F ∈ F, G ∈ G), then |F|·|G| ≤ h(n,k)·(n-1 choose ℓ-1), where h(n,k) = (n-1 choose k-1) - (n-k-1 choose k-1) + 1 is the Hilton-Milner bound.
proof_strategy: First formalize the classical Hilton-Milner theorem as a lemma. Then formalize the notion of cross-intersecting families and non-triviality. The key structural insight from the paper is analyzing 2-cover graphs of cross-intersecting families and bounding the size of families with small minimal covers. The proof proceeds by case analysis on the structure of minimal covers of F and G, showing that non-HM-type configurations yield strictly smaller products when n > 100ℓk².
title: Product Hilton-Milner theorem for large n

description: The theta series of any even positive definite unimodular lattice of rank 8 equals the Eisenstein series E₄. Concretely, for every positive integer n, the number of vectors of norm n in such a lattice equals 240·σ₃(n), where σ₃(n) = Σ_{d|n} d³. This is the foundational special case of the classical Siegel-Weil formula, connecting the theta series of a lattice to an Eisenstein series, and reduces to verifying that the Fourier coefficients of θ_L coincide with those of E₄.
proof_strategy: Two possible routes: (1) Modular route — prove θ_L is a modular form of weight 4 for SL₂(ℤ) via Poisson summation on the lattice, establish that M₄(SL₂(ℤ)) is 1-dimensional spanned by E₄, and match constant terms; (2) Combinatorial route — use the explicit root system of E₈ to compute the theta series coefficients and verify they equal 240·σ₃(n) via the Weyl character formula or direct root system enumeration.
title: Siegel-Weil Identity for the E₈ Lattice Theta Series

description: Every connected bipartite {-1,0,1}-diagonalizable graph on n vertices is a complete bipartite graph K_{n/2, n/2}. This strengthens the paper's theorem that every bipartite {-1,0,1}-diagonalizable graph is regular, and if true, would provide a complete structural characterization connecting the {-1,0,1}-diagonalizability property to classical complete bipartite graph structure.
proof_strategy: Use the paper's structure theorem for {-1,0,1}-diagonalizable graphs of prime order as a base case. For composite orders, leverage the regularity result (Theorem: bipartite implies regular) combined with the eigenvector structure constraints: the {-1,0,1} eigenvector basis forces strong conditions on the adjacency patterns of regular bipartite graphs. A possible approach shows that if G is connected, bipartite, regular, and {-1,0,1}-diagonalizable, then any two vertices in the same part have identical neighbor sets, yielding completeness. Attempt falsification by exhaustive search for small orders using the enumeration data provided.
title: Bipartite {-1,0,1}-diagonalizable graphs are complete bipartite

description: For all positive integers k ≥ 2, n ≥ 1, and 1 ≤ j ≤ n, the symmetric function Δ_{e_j} G(k,n) is Schur positive (i.e., expands with nonnegative coefficients in ℕ[q,t] in the Schur basis) if and only if k divides n, where G(k,n) = Σ_{λ⊢n, λ₁<k} m_λ is the Petrie symmetric function and Δ_{e_j} is the Bergeron–Garsia delta operator applied to e_j. This extends the paper's main result for ∇ = Δ_{e_n} (and its iterates ∇^r) to all elementary symmetric function inputs of the delta operator, establishing that the divisibility criterion governs Schur positivity uniformly across the entire family of delta operators.
domain_bridges: Representation theory of symmetric groups (Schur positivity ↔ graded module existence)
Diagonal harmonics and nabla operator theory
proof_strategy: For the forward direction (k∣n ⟹ Schur positivity): decompose G(k,n) into creation operator images C_α when k∣n, then apply the compositional shuffle theorem framework to express Δ_{e_j} C_α as a positively weighted sum of vertical LLT polynomials, leveraging Grojnowski–Haiman Schur positivity of LLT polynomials. For the converse (k∤n ⟹ not Schur positive): extend the sign-analysis techniques from the paper's nabla case to general Δ_{e_j} by tracking the leading negative Schur coefficients in the Macdonald polynomial expansion of G(k,n) under the delta eigenvalue action, showing that the divisibility obstruction propagates through all delta operators.
title: Delta-Petrie Schur Positivity

description: The fluctuation of the weighted counting function of closed geodesics in homology classes modulo $q$, defined as $\Psi_M(X; q, \alpha) - \Psi_M(X)/q^{2g}$, when normalized by its asymptotic standard deviation $\sqrt{X \log X}$, converges in distribution to a standard normal distribution as $X \to \infty$ and $g \to \infty$. This conjecture extends the paper's computation of the variance ($\sim X \log X$) to a full central limit theorem, analogous to the Gaussian distribution of primes in arithmetic progressions.
proof_strategy: Establish moment bounds for higher-order moments of the fluctuations to apply the method of moments, leveraging the Selberg trace formula on random surfaces and the known variance asymptotic of $X \log X$.
title: Asymptotic Normality of Prime Geodesic Fluctuations on Random Hyperbolic Surfaces

description: For Levenshtein's sequence reconstruction problem with insertion errors, the paper proves the surprising fact that N_q^m(n,1) = N_q^{nm}(n,1) for all alphabet size q and word length n—that is, the minimum number of channels required for unambiguous reconstruction is identical whether repeated outputs are tracked as a multiset or as an unordered set, when exactly one insertion occurs per channel. The conjecture proposes that this equality extends to all insertion counts t >= 1: N_q^m(n,t) = N_q^{nm}(n,t) for all q >= 2, n >= 1, t >= 1.
proof_strategy: Proceed by induction on t, leveraging the t=1 base case proven in the paper. For the inductive step, analyze how the multiset and non-multiset intersection structures of insertion balls decompose when composing t insertions as a sequence of single insertions. The key difficulty is showing that the overlap multiplicities from repeated error patterns cannot create a distinction between the multiset and non-multiset models even when t > 1. A combinatorial double-counting argument on the equivalence classes of insertion error patterns producing identical outputs may suffice.
title: Equality of Multiset and Non-Multiset Reconstruction Numbers for All Insertion Counts

description: For the family of quadratic Dirichlet L-functions L(u, χ_D) where D ranges over squarefree polynomials of odd degree d = 2g+1 in F_q[T], the n-level density of normalized zeros converges to the n-level density of eigenvalue angles of USp(2g) matrices as q → ∞. Specifically, for any Schwartz function f : ℝ^n → ℝ with Fourier transform supported in (-1,1)^n, the family-average of ∑_{distinct i₁,...,i_n} f(θ_{i₁},...,θ_{i_n}) over normalized zero angles θ of L(u,χ_D) converges to ∫_{[0,1]^n} f(x) · W_{n,USp(2g)}(x) dx, where W_{n,USp(2g)} is the symplectic n-level density kernel.
proof_strategy: Adapt the Mason-Snaith ratio conjecture framework to function fields: (1) formalize the explicit formula relating sums over zeros to sums over primes in F_q[T], (2) compute the n-level density via the ratio of L-functions averaged over the family using character sum identities over F_q[T], (3) show the resulting combinatorial expression matches the n-level correlation kernel of USp(2g) eigenvalues computed from the symplectic group's Weyl integration formula, using the restricted Fourier support to control error terms.
title: Symplectic n-level density correspondence for quadratic Dirichlet L-functions over function fields

description: For every integer n ≥ 2, there exists a finite free n-dimensional simplicial Z_2-complex K such that coind(K) = 1 and coind(S(K)) = n+1, demonstrating that the excess of the co-index of a suspension over the lower bound coind(X)+1 can be arbitrarily large.
proof_strategy: Explicitly construct the simplicial Z_2-complex K for each n, prove it is a free Z_2-space, and compute its co-index and the co-index of its suspension using the Borsuk-Ulam theorem and homotopy equivalence arguments.
title: Unbounded Gap Between Co-Index of a Free Z_2-Space and Its Suspension

description: For every positive integer m and every 0 < α < 1/2, there exists a constant C(m,α) > 0 such that for all odd prime powers q and all subsets E ⊆ F_q^{2m}, if |E| ≥ C(m,α) · q^m then the set of nonzero quadratic distances Δ_Q^×(E) = {Q(x−y) : x,y ∈ E} ∩ F_q^× has size greater than α(q−1), where Q(x) = x₁² + ⋯ + x_{2m}². This asserts that subsets of F_q^{2m} of size proportional to q^m determine a positive proportion of all possible nonzero distances, which is the sharp threshold predicted by the Erdős–Falconer conjecture. The current paper achieves this conditionally on a Kloosterman anti-concentration conjecture, and unconditionally achieves the weaker q^{m+1/2} threshold.
proof_strategy: The paper's semidefinite Delsarte framework reduces the conjecture to a uniform L¹ anti-concentration statement for positive convex combinations of classical Kloosterman sums. A complete proof requires either (1) establishing the Kloosterman anti-concentration conjecture—that positive convex combinations of Kloosterman sums K_q(a·t) cannot concentrate in L¹ beyond a universal lower bound proportional to 1/√q—or (2) an entirely new method bypassing the Delsarte/LP framework. The unconditional q^{m+1/2} threshold follows from a second-moment bound on Kloosterman sums (Weil bound), but improving to q^m requires overcoming the fundamental barrier that individual Kloosterman columns can nearly cancel.
title: Erdős–Falconer Distance Conjecture in Even Finite Field Dimensions

description: Every t-perfect graph is 4-colorable. The discovery of t-perfect graphs with chromatic number 4 demonstrates that this bound would be tight. Although recent breakthroughs have established the first finite upper bounds on the chromatic number of t-perfect graphs (currently 186), a wide gap remains between the lower bound of 4 and the upper bound, making this a central open problem in polyhedral combinatorics.
proof_strategy: Further refine the structural analysis of graphs avoiding odd wheels as t-minors and their odd cycle intersections, potentially leveraging the integer decomposition property of the stable set polytope or developing new leveling arguments to progressively reduce the chromatic upper bound from 186 down to 4.
title: t-Perfect Graph 4-Colorability Conjecture

description: For every loopless matroid M on finite ground set E and every Feichtner–Yuzvinsky building set G containing the top flat E, the K-polynomial of the integral tangent class T^Z_{M,G} ∈ K_Z(M,G) equals the Hilbert series of the Chow ring A*(M,G). Concretely, P^K(T^Z_{M,G}, t) = Hilb(A*(M,G), t) as polynomials in Z[t]. This is the central P^K=Hilb identity (Theorem A, property 2) of the paper, connecting the K-theoretic tangent class to the cohomological Hilbert series.
domain_bridges: graded ring homomorphisms between K-ring and Chow ring
proof_strategy: First formalize loopless matroids, Feichtner-Yuzvinsky building sets, the graded integral K-ring K_Z(M,G) with its alpha-generators, and the Chow ring A*(M,G) with its Bergman fan presentation. Construct the integral tangent class via the quotient/theta-machinery of Sections 4-5. Then prove P^K=Hilb by establishing that the K-ring Chern character ch_K maps T^Z_{M,G} to the Todd class whose pushforward recovers the Hilbert series, mirroring the classical HRR argument adapted to the combinatorial setting.
title: Hirzebruch–Riemann–Roch Identity for the Integral Tangent Class of Matroids

description: For any subset A ⊆ [N] containing no harmonic triple (distinct a, b, c ∈ A with 2/a = 1/b + 1/c), the density |A|/N → 0 as N → ∞. Formally: ∀ ε > 0, ∃ N₀, ∀ N ≥ N₀, every A ⊆ {1,...,N} with no harmonic triple satisfies |A| ≤ ε·N. This is the reciprocal analogue of Roth's theorem on 3-AP-free sets, posed as Question 1 in the paper. The paper's construction yields sets of size ≫ N·exp(−C√(log log N)), so a positive resolution would need new upper-bound techniques beyond Roth-type methods, since the reciprocal map x ↦ 1/x is not additive.
proof_strategy: Adapt density-increment or energy-based methods (Bloom-Sisask, Kelley-Meka) to the multiplicative/reciprocal setting. Key obstacle: the map n ↦ n⁻¹ mod q is nonlinear, so arithmetic regularity lemmas don't directly apply. A promising approach: show that a positive-density set A ⊆ [N] must contain many 'approximate' harmonic triples, then use a stability argument to upgrade to exact ones. Alternatively, develop a Fourier-analytic framework for the equation 2bc = a(b+c) over the integers, treating the quadratic constraint via sieve methods.
title: Reciprocal Roth Conjecture: Harmonic-Triple-Free Sets Have Density Zero

description: For any prime power $q$, there exists a cyclic sequence of length $q^3(q^2+q+1)$ over the alphabet of affine points and $1$-subspaces in $\mathbb{F}_q^3$ such that every affine plane in $\mathbb{F}_q^3$ is represented exactly once by a sliding window of length three. The window encodes an affine plane $w + \langle u_1, u_2 \rangle$ via a triple of mixed affine points and direction classes (e.g., $(w, [u_1], [u_2])$ or $(w, w+u_1, w+u_2)$). This extends the paper's construction which currently holds for $n \ge 4$.
proof_strategy: Adapt the local-to-global frame decomposition and gluing technique from the $n \ge 4$ case by constructing explicit local cycles on frame configurations in $\mathbb{F}_q^3$ and finding a Hamiltonian cycle in the corresponding transition graph, overcoming the restricted dimensionality that prevents the standard layered frame decomposition from working directly.
title: Universal Cycles for Affine Planes in $\mathbb{F}_q^3$

description: The paper proves that every circular Hessenberg pair satisfies the tridiagonal relations (Lee's conjecture). The converse remains open: among all Hessenberg pairs on a nonzero finite-dimensional vector space, exactly the circular ones satisfy the tridiagonal relations. That is, a Hessenberg pair (A, A*) satisfies the tridiagonal relations if and only if it is circular (i.e., each acts on an eigenbasis of the other in a circular Hessenberg fashion, meaning the top-right corner entry is nonzero and every other entry above the superdiagonal is zero).
proof_strategy: The forward direction is the content of the paper (proving Lee's conjecture). For the converse, suppose a Hessenberg pair satisfies the tridiagonal relations. Use the tridiagonal relations to derive constraints on the matrix entries of each operator acting on the other's eigenbasis. Show that the vanishing conditions above the superdiagonal (except the top-right corner) and the nonvanishing of the top-right corner follow from the tridiagonal relations combined with the Hessenberg structure. This may involve analyzing the recurrence relations imposed by the tridiagonal relations on the entries of the Hessenberg matrices and showing that non-circular Hessenberg pairs violate these relations.
title: Circular Hessenberg pairs are characterized by the tridiagonal relations

catalog_references: Barát–Blázsik–Damásdi (2019): Decomposition of subcubic outerplanar graphs and the crumby coloring conjecture
Thomassen conjecture on red-blue partitions of 3-connected cubic graphs
Wegner conjecture on chromatic numbers of squares of planar graphs
Bellitto et al. counterexample to Thomassen's conjecture for 3-connected cubic graphs
description: Formalize that every finite simple subcubic outerplanar graph admits a crumby coloring: a red-blue vertex partition where the blue vertices induce a subgraph of maximum degree at most one, and the red vertices induce a subgraph with minimum degree at least one and no induced path on four vertices (P₄). This resolves the Barát–Blázsik–Damásdi conjecture and extends their result from 2-connected to all subcubic outerplanar graphs. The proof introduces a rooted grammatical decomposition of subcubic outerplanar graphs into rooted branches and two-terminal path fragments, extends crumby colorings to crumby-admissible colorings that permit temporary defects at boundary vertices, and reduces the inductive verification to checking an explicit finite family of certificates.
domain_bridges: Graph minor theory ↔ constrained 2-colorability (outerplanarity as a forbidden-minor condition enabling the grammatical decomposition)
Formal grammars ↔ graph decomposition (rooted grammar producing subcubic outerplanar graphs from branches and path fragments)
Computer-verified certificate checking ↔ combinatorial existence proofs (finite certificate closure verified by a stand-alone checker)
proof_strategy: First formalize subcubic outerplanar graphs and the crumby coloring property. Then formalize the rooted grammatical decomposition: every finite simple subcubic outerplanar graph decomposes recursively via rooted branches and two-terminal path fragments, with cyclic blocks handled by deleting the root. Define crumby-admissible colorings that allow temporary isolated red vertices at boundary locations (the root of a rooted branch, or the two terminals of a path fragment). Prove by induction on the grammar that every decomposed graph admits a crumby-admissible coloring, reducing to verifying an explicit finite family of lower certificates (boundary types and root states). The finite verification that the certificate family is closed under all decomposition steps and that every completed branch contains a final-legal root state can be automated via decidable computation, while the structural reductions and certificate-induction principle are proved by hand.
title: Every subcubic outerplanar graph admits a crumby coloring

description: The paper proves that for any fixed c ∈ [1, √2), there exist finite metric spaces requiring exponentially large finitely presented c-approximations of the Vietoris-Rips filtration, and that for any c ≥ 1, superlinear size is necessary. This conjecture posits that √2 is the sharp threshold between exponential and polynomial approximability: for every fixed c ≥ √2, there exists a polynomial p_c such that every finite metric space X admits a finitely presented c-approximation to VR(X) of size at most p_c(|X|). This would yield a complete dichotomy—exponential below √2, polynomial at or above √2—matching the natural geometric breakpoint where the Rips complex becomes the full simplex on any metric space with all distances ≤ 2r.
domain_bridges: computational complexity theory (threshold phenomena in approximability)
proof_strategy: Establish the upper bound by constructing polynomial-size approximations for c ≥ √2. The key insight should be that at approximation factor √2, the homotopy interleaving relaxation is strong enough to allow collapse of high-dimensional simplices that are forced in the exact filtration. A potential approach: (1) Show that for c ≥ √2, any finite metric space can be embedded into a space of bounded doubling dimension with distortion at most √2, then invoke Sheehy-type sparse approximation results; (2) Alternatively, directly construct a filtration that is homotopy-interleaved with VR(X) at factor √2 using controlled local collapses whose combinatorial complexity is polynomially bounded.
title: The √2-Threshold Conjecture for Rips Filtration Approximation

description: Conjecture that the optimal exponential rate at the Dirac boundary established for n/2-regular graphs extends to all graphs with minimum degree at least n/2. Specifically, every n-vertex graph G with minimum degree δ(G) ≥ n/2 satisfies Cyc(G) ≥ 2^{(1-o(1))n}, which is sharp up to a subexponential factor as witnessed by K_{n/2,n/2}.
proof_strategy: Adapt the absorbing method and robustness of Hamiltonicity under minimum degree conditions. Show that any graph with δ(G) ≥ n/2 contains a robust spanning structure (e.g., a Hamilton-connected subgraph or a suitable power of a Hamilton cycle) that guarantees a positive fraction of vertex subsets induce Hamiltonian subgraphs. Count subsets via expansion or balanced bipartition arguments mirroring the regular case.
title: Dirac Boundary Cyclic Subset Bound for Minimum Degree Graphs

description: For any k ≥3 and 1≤ℓ<k, and any two accumulation points α, β in Π^k_ℓ, there exists a transfer function f such that f(α) = β.
proof_strategy: Construct a tree suspension parameterized to target specific densities, demonstrating that tree structures can interpolate between any pair of accumulation points.
title: Universality of Transfer Functions Among Accumulation Points

description: For any quadratic polynomial P ∈ ℤ[x] with positive leading coefficient that is not a constant times the square of a linear polynomial, the number of quadruples (n₁, n₂, n₃, n₄) ∈ [1, N]⁴ such that P(n₁)P(n₂)P(n₃)P(n₄) is a perfect square is asymptotic to c_P N² (log N)² as N → ∞, where c_P > 0 is a constant depending on P. This conjecture captures the paucity phenomenon where diagonal solutions (pairwise products forming squares) dominate, and the (log N)² factor arises from the rich structure of Pell–Fermat equations associated with P.
proof_strategy: 1. Parametrize diagonal solutions via pairs (n₁, n₂) with P(n₁)P(n₂) = □. 2. Use the theory of Pell–Fermat equations to show the number of such pairs is ∼ c_P N log N. 3. Square this to get the diagonal contribution ∼ c_P² N² (log N)². 4. Apply Evertse–Silverman bounds on S-unit equations to show non-diagonal solutions are o(N² (log N)²). 5. Combine with Hooley's sieve methods to handle the square-free condition in the Rademacher case.
title: Asymptotic for Square Products of Quadratic Polynomial Values

catalog_references: Schur positivity of nabla on Petrie symmetric functions
description: For all integers k ≥ 1, n ≥ 1, and r ≥ 1, the symmetric function ∇^r applied to the Petrie symmetric function G(k,n) is Schur positive if and only if k divides n. This conjecture formalizes the main result of the paper, establishing a precise equivalence between divisibility and Schur positivity.
proof_strategy: Prove both directions: (1) If k divides n, then ∇^r G(k,n) is Schur positive by constructing a combinatorial model (e.g., parking functions or labeled trees) whose Frobenius characteristic matches the symmetric function. (2) If k does not divide n, show non-negativity fails by finding a partition λ where the Schur coefficient of s_λ in ∇^r G(k,n) is negative, possibly via representation-theoretic obstructions or explicit computation of expanded forms.
title: Schur Positivity of ∇^r G(k,n) if and only if k divides n

description: For any finite set V partitioned into d+1 disjoint color classes U_1,...,U_{d+1}, and any map A:V→ℝ^d such that 0 lies in the convex cone generated by each A(U_i), the simplicial complex K of colorful transversals whose cone contains 0 is (d-2)-connected, i.e., \tilde{H}_i(K)=0 for all i≤d-2. This conjecture extends the (d-1)-Leray property from the classical colorful Carathéodory setting to cone configurations and can be falsified by exhibiting a counterexample with non‑trivial homology in degree d-1.
proof_strategy: Homology vanishing via Nerve theorem and spectral sequence analysis of the colored complex
title: Conjecture on (d-2)-Connectivity of the Cone-Colorful Carathéodory Support Complex

description: For every inclusion-free hypergraph H on n vertices, there exists an edge offset function f : H → ℝ such that the number of isolating weight assignments w ∈ [d]^n equals the lower bound n * ∑_{j=0}^{d-1} j^{n-1}. This would show that the bound proved in the paper is not only globally tight (achieved by the singleton hypergraph with f = 0) but also tight for each individual hypergraph when the offsets are chosen appropriately.
proof_strategy: Use the transformation technique from Ta-Shma (2015) and the paper's proof to construct suitable edge offsets f for a given H. One approach is to show that for any inclusion-free H, there is a weight-preserving bijection between its isolating assignments (with some f) and those of the singleton hypergraph, or to inductively build f by adding edges and adjusting offsets to maintain the exact count of isolating assignments.
title: Tightness of the Isolation Lemma bound for arbitrary edge offsets

proof_strategy: The proof would combine the constructive lower‑bound method from the paper (building dense families of hypergraphs containing many balanced triangles) with an improved Lovász‑Local‑Lemma or density‑increment argument to obtain matching upper bounds.  In a Lean formalization one would first define r‑uniform hypergraphs, the family \u03c6 of balanced triangles, the notion of an \u03c6‑coloring, and the function \u03c7^r_F(d).  Then one would encode the lower‑bound construction as a series of lemmas about degree growth, and the upper‑bound argument as a recursive greedy coloring algorithm together with a potential‑function analysis.  The final theorem would assert the existence of constants C1, C2 and a threshold N such that the inequalities above hold for all d ≥ N.
title: Exact asymptotic growth of \u03c7^r_F(d) for the balanced‑triangle family

description: There exists an effectively computable constant γ > 0 such that for every c ∈ [1, √2), there exists an infinite family of finite metric spaces {Xₙ} indexed by n ∈ ℕ where any finitely presented c-approximation to the Vietoris-Rips filtration VR(Xₙ) requires at least 2^(γ·n) simplices, and moreover γ can be taken to satisfy γ = γ(c) with lim_{c→√2⁻} γ(c) = 0.
domain_bridges: Formal verification of persistent homology algorithms
proof_strategy: 1. Construct an explicit infinite family of finite metric spaces Xₙ (e.g., using ℓ₁-spheres or Hamming cube constructions) with controlled geometric properties. 2. Prove that these spaces have unbounded doubling dimension. 3. Use combinatorial arguments to show that any c-approximation must encode sufficient information to distinguish between exponentially many distinct metric configurations. 4. Establish the quantitative bound on γ(c) by analyzing the homomorphism density needed in the approximation maps. 5. Verify the limit behavior as c approaches √2 from below using asymptotic analysis.
title: Explicit exponential lower bound for Vietoris-Rips approximations below √2 threshold

description: For every d-regular simple graph G on n vertices, there exists a spanning subgraph H such that for each i ∈ {0,…,d}, the count m(H,i) of vertices with degree i in H satisfies |m(H,i) - n/(d+1)| ≤ 2. This is the original conjecture of Alon and Wei, proven in the cited paper only for fixed d or for d ≤ n^{1/12−ε}.
proof_strategy: Initialize H via the threshold random subgraph model (independent uniform labels, keep edge uv if x_u+x_v ≥ 1). This yields asymptotic degree counts. Then apply a sequence of single-edge switches (swaps along anti-diagonals) to drive the twofold prefix norm of the degree-count error to zero while preserving the parity constraint. A full proof would need a uniform edge-atom probability bound valid for all d ≤ n and stronger concentration of the prefix norm, possibly via spectral graph theory or martingale methods.
title: Alon–Wei Conjecture for Arbitrary Regular Graphs

catalog_references: Corneil et al. 'Cographs: recognition and applications' (1981)
description: The class of cographs (Forb(P₄)) is generalized spectrally closed: if G is a cograph and H is generalized cospectral with G (i.e., G and H have the same adjacency spectrum and the same complement spectrum), then H must also be a cograph. This extends the paper's result for threshold graphs (Forb(2K₂, P₄, C₄)) to the larger class of cographs.
proof_strategy: Apply the paper's β-closed walk framework and linear programming approach to search for a walk-realizable {P₄}-supporter. If such a supporter exists, the LP feasibility problem will certify generalized spectral closedness. If no supporter exists, attempt to construct a counterexample by finding a cograph G and a non-cograph H with identical generalized spectra, possibly using the paper's induced-subgraph expansion formulas for β-closed walk counts.
title: Cographs are generalized spectrally closed

description: Conjecture: For every integer t ≥ 2 there exists a constant C_t > 0 such that every K_{2,t}-free graph with average degree at least C_t h^2 contains an induced subdivision of K_h. This would remove the Ω(h^2 log^7 h) factor established in the paper and confirm that the exponent 2 is optimal without logarithmic penalties.
proof_strategy: Use a strengthened sparse regularity lemma for K_{2,t}-free graphs to obtain a regular bipartite subgraph with strong expansion, then embed an induced subdivision of K_h via greedy path routing that exploits the forbidden K_{2,t} to control common neighborhoods and avoid extra edges, eliminating the logarithmic overcounting present in the original proof.
title: Logarithm-free bound for induced clique subdivisions in K_{2,t}-free graphs

description: For any permutation π ∈ S_n, let G_π be its inversion graph and c(G_π) its cyclomatic number (|E|-|V|+components). We conjecture that the total number of occurrences of the permutation patterns 321 and 3412 in π is at most c(G_π). This extends the paper's claim that the inversion graph bounds each pattern count individually.
proof_strategy: Utilize the reduced-word edge ordering from the paper: first-occurrence edges form a spanning forest, repeated edges correspond to cyclomatic number. Show each 321 or 3412 pattern forces at least one independent cycle or repeated edge; induct on cyclomatic number by deleting leaf vertices of the inversion graph, using the proven forest case where both pattern counts are zero.
title: Sum of 321 and 3412 pattern counts bounded by cyclomatic number

description: Every exotic Diophantine triple in $\mathbb{R}[X]$ with a nonconstant element and containing the element 1 must be of the form $\{k^2-1,\ (k+1)^2-1,\ 1\}$ for some nonconstant $k \in \mathbb{R}[X]$. This conjecture asserts that the family provided in the paper's introduction exhausts all such triples.
proof_strategy: Adapt the regularity theorem approach from Filipin-Jurasić to characterize all possible triples containing 1. Show that the conditions imposed by the seven-square requirement force the elements to align with the given family structure, possibly via analyzing the factorization properties of the polynomials and leveraging the constraints imposed by the squares.
title: All exotic Diophantine triples in $\mathbb{R}[X]$ containing 1 are of the form $\{k^2-1, (k+1)^2-1, 1\}$ for some nonconstant $k \in \mathbb{R}[X]$

catalog_references: Lovász's box complex lower bound χ(G) ≥ coind(B(G))+2
Simonyi–Tardos–Vrécica question on co-index growth under suspension
description: For every integers d ≥ 2 and c with 1 ≤ c ≤ d, there exists a finite free simplicial Z2-complex K of dimension d such that coind(K) = c and coind(suspension K) = d + 1. This generalizes the paper's result (which proves the case c = 1 for all d ≥ 2) and would show that the upper bound coind(S(K)) ≤ dim(K)+1 is sharp for every possible starting co-index c, achieving maximal excess d - c.
domain_bridges: graph chromatic number bounds via box complexes
proof_strategy: Use the paper's explicit construction of K_n (dim n, coind 1, coind of suspension n+1) as a base block. For a given c, take the join of K_{d-c+1} with an antipodal sphere S^{c-2} (which has coind c-2 and dimension c-2). The join of free Z2-complexes satisfies dim(X*Y)=dim(X)+dim(Y)+1 and coind(X*Y) ≥ coind(X)+coind(Y)+1, yielding a complex of dimension d and coind at least c. Show by induction on the simplicial structure that equality holds and that suspension of the join realizes coind d+1, possibly via an equivariant homeomorphism Σ(X*Y) ≅ ΣX * ΣY and the known coind of ΣK_{d-c+1}=d-c+2 and ΣS^{c-2}=S^{c-1} (coind c-1). The resulting lower bound gives coind ≥ d+1, and dimension bounds force equality. Formalize simplicial join and suspension in Lean 4.
title: Sharp maximal excess of co-index under suspension for all feasible starting co-indices

description: The paper proves that for any d-regular graph G on n vertices with d ≤ n^{1/12-ε} and any integer vector q=(q_0,…,q_d) satisfying ∑ q_i = n, ∑ i q_i ≡ 0 (mod 2), and |q_i - n/(d+1)| ≤ 1 for all i, there exists a spanning subgraph H ⊆ G with m(H,i)=q_i exactly. We conjecture that this exact prescription holds for every d-regular graph on n vertices and every such admissible q, i.e., without the restriction d ≤ n^{1/12-ε}.
proof_strategy: Refine the anti-diagonal edge-move correction step by replacing the twofold prefix norm bound with a potential that remains O(d^2√n) or smaller for d up to n^{1/2} or beyond, possibly using iterative absorption, balanced random adjustments, or hypergraph container methods to control the lattice cost uniformly for all d.
title: Exact degree-count prescription without polynomial-range restriction

description: For every prime power q and every pair of integers n, k with 2·k ≤ n, any constant‑dimension Schubert subspace code of minimum subspace distance 2·k satisfies |C| ≤ S(q, n, k), where S(q, n, k) denotes the maximum size of a partial k‑spread in PG(n‑1, q). Moreover, equality holds if and only if the code is a spread code (i.e., the codewords form a partition of the ambient vector space). This conjecture is falsifiable: a single counterexample— a Schubert code of distance 2·k whose cardinality strictly exceeds S(q, n, k)— would refute it.
proof_strategy: combinatorial counting via chromatic and clique obstructions in powers of q‑Johnson graphs, combined with a double‑counting argument relating code size to partial spreads
title: No Schubert code can exceed the size of a maximal partial spread in the extremal distance case

description: We conjecture that for any integers r≥2, s≥2 and any n‑ vertex r‑uniform hypergraph H with matching number ν(H)< s, the spectral radius ρ(H) (defined as the Perron‑Frobenius eigenvalue of its adjacency tensor) satisfies ρ(H)≤ρ(十₁(s‑1)(n)), where 十₁(a)(n) denotes the family of all r‑subsets of [n] intersecting a fixed set of size a (the “star” hypergraph). Moreover, equality holds if and only if H is isomorphic to 十₁(s‑1)(n). This is a spectral analogue of the Erdős‑Matching Conjecture, extending the result of the paper to all n (not just “sufficiently large”) and providing a precise, formalizable statement suitable for verification in Lean 4.
domain_bridges: Lean formalization of hypergraphs and spectral radius
proof_strategy:
1. Formalize r‑uniform hypergraphs as subsets of ℓ[n] {r} in Lean.
2. Define the adjacency tensor and the spectral radius via the Perron‑Frobenius eigenvalue (using existing Lean spectral theory libraries).
3. Implement the shifting operation and prove its monotonicity for the spectral radius.
4. Derive spectral upper bounds via hypergraph decomposition and tensor variational formulas.
5. Analyse the structure of shifted‑saturated hypergraphs with ν(H)< s, showing they must be exactly 十₁(s‑1)(n).
6. Extend the bound to arbitrary hypergraphs using stability arguments.
7. Formalise the conjecture as a theorem in Lean, with auxiliary lemmas for matching number, star hypergraph construction, and isomorphism testing.
title: Spectral Extremal Conjecture for Hypergraphs with Bounded Matching Number

description: Conjecture that any directed strongly regular graph on 108 vertices must have degree k belonging to the set {11,14,22,23,25,34,38,39,41,42,46}. Equivalently, no such graph exists with a degree outside this set.
proof_strategy: Search computationally over all parameter tuples (k,λ,μ,ν) that satisfy the feasibility conditions for a directed strongly regular graph on 108 vertices, and verify that none are viable unless k is in the listed set; then provide a theoretical argument using the parameter equations and transitivity constraints to show that k must belong to that set.
title: Conjecture on the possible degrees of directed strongly regular graphs on 108 vertices

description: We conjecture that the hereditary class of cographs, i.e., graphs with no induced path on four vertices (P4), is generalized spectrally closed: any graph generalized cospectral with a cograph must itself be a cograph. This extends the paper's proven results for threshold graphs (Forb(2K2,P4,C4)) and chain graphs.
proof_strategy: Utilize the paper's β-closed walk expansion and the sufficient condition via a walk-realizable {P4}-supporter. Reduce the search to a linear programming feasibility problem for coefficients of β-closed walk counts. Compute a concrete finite witness (e.g., with bounded walk length) satisfying the LP, then formalize the induced-subgraph expansion and supporter criterion in Lean 4 to verify the implication.
title: Generalized spectral closedness of cographs (Forb(P4))

description: Let Sh_G be a Shimura variety of Hodge type with μ-ordinary Mantovan Igusa variety Ig_μ. Let D = ⊕_{i=1}^n D_i be the graded algebra of rank one Maass--Shimura differential operators on Ig_μ. Conjecture: There exists an explicit n-dimensional commutative formal group F_D such that the action of D integrates to an action of F_D on Ig_μ, and the coordinate ring of F_D is canonically isomorphic to the symmetric algebra Sym(D) equipped with a specific coproduct structure determined by the Hodge embedding data. Moreover, this isomorphism is equivariant for the natural action of the derived Hecke algebra H^*(K_p, G) where K_p is a hyperspecial maximal subgroup.
proof_strategy: Construct the formal group via the universal property of the tangent space of Ig_μ, use the Hodge type embedding to identify the differential operators with components of the logarithm map, then prove the coproduct compatibility by analyzing the group structure on Ig_μ via p-adic Fourier theory and the Mantovan correspondence.
title: Explicit Formal Group Integrating p-adic Maass--Shimura Operators for Hodge Type Shimura Varieties

catalog_references: Buchanan et al., Journal of Graph Theory 2026
description: We conjecture that for all integers $r\ge2$ and $n\ge r+1$, the minimum number $b_{r+1}(n+1)$ of complete $(r+1)\!$-partite $(r+1)\!$-graphs needed to odd‑cover the complete $(r+1)\!$-uniform hypergraph $K_{n+1}^{(r+1)}$ equals the minimum number $b_{r}(n)$ of complete $r$\!‑partite $r$\!‑graphs needed to odd‑cover $K_n^{(r)}$. In symbols, $$b_{r+1}(n+1)=b_{r}(n)\,.$$
domain_bridges: construction of odd covers via bipartite subgraph complementations
proof_strategy: Extend the proof of $b_3(n+1)=b_2(n)$ to arbitrary uniformity.  Develop a systematic 'shifting' construction that lifts an optimal odd cover of $K_n^{(r)}$ to an odd cover of $K_{n+1}^{(r+1)}$ of the same size, showing $b_{r+1}(n+1)\le b_r(n)$.  Simultaneously, apply the $\mathbb{F}_2$ rank bound $b_r(G)\ge r_2(A_G)/2$ to complete $(r+1)\!$-uniform hypergraphs to obtain $b_{r+1}(n+1)\ge b_r(n)$.  Together these give equality.  The combinatorial details involve analysing the adjacency tensors of complete hypergraphs over $\mathbb{F}_2$ and using induction on $r$.
title: Recursive relation for odd cover numbers of complete hypergraphs

description: The paper proves that for c≥2, the number of Dyck paths of semilength n=cm+r-1 whose column-residue class sums are equal (c-balanced) is the Raney number Raney_{c+1,r}(m). We conjecture a refinement: the number of such c-balanced paths with exactly k peaks equals the rational Narayana number N_{(c+1,m,r)}(k) (equivalently, the peak distribution matches that of (c+1)-ary trees with r marked nodes). This is falsifiable by explicit enumeration for small parameters.
proof_strategy: Derive the bivariate generating function for c-balanced Dyck paths weighted by peak count using the kernel method extended from the paper, and show it coincides with the known rational Narayana generating function. Alternatively, construct an explicit bijection to marked (c+1)-ary trees that preserves peaks, potentially via the cycle lemma on Raney sequences.
title: Peak refinement of c-balanced Dyck path enumeration

description: For the Wenger graph W_5(q) (the k=5 case where the girth conjecture is known to hold), any f-degree fault tolerant 9-spanner must have at least (1/20) * f^(4/5) * n^(6/5) edges for all prime powers q ≥ 2 and all f ≤ q^4 / 10, where n = 2q^5 is the number of vertices. This strengthens the asymptotic Ω(f^(1-1/k) n^(1+1/k)) lower bound of the paper with an explicit constant factor for the largest known explicit construction.
proof_strategy: Use the Szabó-Conlon reinterpretation of Wenger graphs as norm graphs over finite fields. Analyze the number of edge-disjoint paths of length ≤ 9 between vertex pairs that must survive any f-degree fault set. Apply a double counting argument on the incidence matrix of paths versus edges, optimizing the constant via the eigenvalue distribution of the associated algebraic variety.
title: Explicit Constant Factor for Wenger Graph DFT Spanner Lower Bound

catalog_references: Algorithms for the Odd Cycle Transversal Problem in Special Classes of Graphs (Parameterized Settings)
description: This conjecture posits that the Odd Cycle Transversal problem is solvable in polynomial time for graphs with bounded induced-$\mathcal{H}$-packing treewidth when $\mathcal{H} = \{P_3\}$, providing a parameterized framework for algorithmic meta-theorems in graph classes defined by forbidden induced $P_3$ subgraphs.
proof_strategy: Construct a fixed-parameter tractable (FPT) algorithm using the tree decomposition structure, where decomposition size is bounded by a function of the induced-$\mathcal{H}$-packing treewidth, and iteratively prune odd cycles via bag-wise constraints.
title: Fixed-Parameter Algorithmic Consequences of Bounded Induced-$\mathcal{H}$-Packing Treewidth for $P_3$-Free Graphs

description: For each of the 106 reduction type families for genus 2 curves over local fields with p ≠ 2, there exists a computable bijection between cluster pictures (as defined in the paper) and reduction types. Specifically, each cluster picture in the complete list associated to a reduction type corresponds to exactly one Weierstrass model, and every smooth projective genus 2 curve over K with that reduction type realizes each of its listed cluster pictures through some minimal Weierstrass equation. Moreover, the valuation of the discriminant and the Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer fudge factor are constant across all Weierstrass models realizing the same cluster picture.
domain_bridges: Elliptic curve Kodaira classification → Genus 2 Namikawa-Ueno classification
proof_strategy: Establish the bijection by constructing an explicit algorithm: (1) Given a genus 2 curve with specified reduction type, produce its cluster picture via the dual graph of the special fiber; (2) Given a cluster picture, construct a Weierstrass model realizing it; (3) Prove that different Weierstrass models with the same cluster picture have identical discriminant valuations and BSD fudge factors using Tate's uniformization theory and semistable reduction techniques. The key is showing the combinatorial data in cluster pictures completely determines the arithmetic invariants.
title: Cluster Picture Bijection Conjecture for Genus 2 Curves

description: For the triangular lattice dimer model, the marginal polynomial obtained by restricting the characteristic polynomial to any boundary side of the Newton polygon has only real roots. This generalizes the proven result for the bipartite case and provides a concrete conjecture that can be tested computationally for small tori and formally verified in Lean.
proof_strategy: Establish a correspondence between the roots of marginal polynomials and equilibrium measures on the amoeba boundary. Use the explicit factorization results from the paper as base cases, then apply perturbation arguments and the preservation of real-rootedness under the local moves. Leverage the relationship between primitive edge vectors and zig-zag path homology classes to control root locations. Connect to Mikhalkin's correspondence theorem for tropical curves.
title: Real-rootedness of marginal polynomials for non-bipartite dimer models

description: This conjecture investigates whether a novel tensor decomposition strategy can systematically reduce computational complexity while preserving norm bounds, thereby enabling tighter spectral gap analysis for Erdős-Rényi hypergraphs.
proof_strategy: Develop a hypergraph-specific tensor decomposition variant that explicitly controls both atomic norms and spectral properties through randomized tensor trains construction.
title: Optimizing Tensor Decomposition for Spectral Gaps in Random Hypergraphs

description: For any integers c ≥ 2 and 1 ≤ r ≤ c, there exists a bijection between the set of c‑balanced Dyck paths of semilength n = c·m + r – 1 and the set of (c+1)-ary rooted trees with m internal nodes and exactly r leaves. Consequently, the number of such Dyck paths equals the Raney number Raney_{c+1,r}(m).
proof_strategy: Construct an explicit combinatorial bijection using the standard encoding of Dyck paths as lattice paths and (c+1)-ary trees, then verify that the class‑sum condition (equal weight per residue class) is preserved under the correspondence.
title: Existence of a bijection between c‑balanced Dyck paths and (c+1)-ary trees with prescribed leaf count

description: We conjecture that for any field F and integers n ≥ m ≥ 0, d ≥ 0, the field‑independent filtration of Δ^(n,m)Sym^dE described in the paper yields graded pieces whose characters are exactly the quantum binomial coefficients appearing in the product rule (Rel2) for Lusztig’s quantum Cartan elements. In particular, the i‑th quotient is isomorphic to Δ^(n‑i,m‑i)Sym^(d‑i)E and its formal character equals s_(n‑i,m‑i) ∘ s_(d‑i).
proof_strategy: Use the symmetric functions model for Weyl modules (as in the paper) to prove by induction on d that the filtration is functorial and that successive quotients have characters given by the plethystic product s_(n‑i,m‑i) ∘ s_(d‑i). The key step is to establish a bijection between the standard basis of the graded pieces and the combinatorial descriptions of the quantum binomial coefficients, mirroring the proof of the product rule (Rel2).
title: Categorifying the quantum binomial product rule via filtrations of plethystic modules

description: We conjecture that for any integers r > s ≥ 3, the minimal possible K_r-density among graphons with prescribed K_s-density λ is given by the classical multipartite edge-to-clique profile re‑parametrised by λ, and that the stability theorem holds for the whole range of λ (including the endpoint λ = 0). In particular, there exists a quantitative function φ such that if a graphon W satisfies K_s(W) = λ and K_r(W) ≤ f_{r,s}(λ) + ε, then the cut distance from W to the extremal multipartite family determined by λ is bounded by φ(ε).
domain_bridges: Graphons and cut distance formalization in proof assistants
proof_strategy: Build on the existing proof of the higher‑order clique density theorem to extend the analysis to the zero‑density endpoint. Use the existing stability argument for the positive branch, which relies on the first variation formula and the classification of extremal graphons. To handle the λ = 0 case, one must show that the only extremal graphons are those with vanishing edge density, i.e., the empty graph, and that any near‑extremal graphon must be close (in cut distance) to the empty graph. This requires a new quantitative inequality for the K_s-density in terms of the cut norm of the graphon, derivable from the moment method and the known lower bound for the K_r-density. The resulting φ(ε) can be taken linear in ε. Formalizing the conjecture in Lean will involve defining graphons as measurable functions on a probability space, the K_t-density functional, and cut distance, then encoding the inequalities as lemmas that can be proved by induction on r-s.
title: Higher-order clique density stability conjecture

description: Conjecture that any n‑vertex graph whose minimum degree is at least n/2 contains at least (1−o(1))·2^n cyclic subsets, i.e. the number of vertex subsets that induce a Hamiltonian cycle is exponential with base 2 and only a subexponential loss.

title: Almost all subsets are cyclic in Dirac graphs

description: For every first-order formula φ with k alternating quantifiers over vertex tuples and unary vertex weights w: V → ℕ, there exists a finite graph G with initial token placement and movement budget b such that the optimal achievable value exceeds any prescribed threshold t if and only if φ is satisfiable in the standard model of arithmetic. This establishes a tight correspondence between FO definability of value functions and computational threshold behavior in solution discovery.

Token sliding reconfiguration ↔ optimization value realization
proof_strategy: Construct a reduction from FO satisfiability to the threshold decision problem by encoding quantifier alternation as iterative value maximization steps. Show that each existential quantifier corresponds to adding vertices that can achieve values above t, while universal quantifiers correspond to adversarial weight assignments. Use Ehrenfeucht-Fraïssé games to establish that non-equivalence of FO formulas manifests as distinct threshold behaviors.
